1+;; census.lg — structurize census for a let-go program.
2+;;
3+;; For every lowerable fn-unit in a corpus (what ir.passes.pipeline/analyze-ns-forms
4+;; harvests: top-level defn/defn-/(def NAME (fn ...)), macros excluded, one unit per
5+;; arity) run the front half of the IR pipeline a WasmGC backend would sit on:
6+;;
7+;; expand-all -> ir.build/build-fn -> ir.passes.pipeline/optimize-fn -> ir.structurize/structurize
8+;;
9+;; and record where it stops. Nothing is evaluated or interned (same discipline as
10+;; scripts/ir-stress.lg, whose file-loading recipe this copies). Also emits, for
11+;; every unit that built, the live-op histogram, the per-value type split and the
12+;; closure/try/dot/set-var/tail-call/recur-fn flags the backend plan needs.
13+;;
14+;; Usage:
15+;; LG_SOURCE_PATHS=<root> lg census.lg <root> <out.tsv> <file-relative-to-root>...
16+;;
17+;; (os/args carries the lg flags too, so args are located by the script name, as
18+;; dev/emit-wasm-probe/reach.lg does.)
19+;;
20+;; Output TSV columns:
21+;; file name arity status bucket msg fallbacks nvals int float bool unknown other flags ops types data-types arith gotos
22+;; arity is "1" (single), "mN" (arity N of a multi-arity defn), or "inner:<parent-arity>/<path>"
23+;; for a nested fn* — build-fn builds those as :fn-template consts inside the parent
24+;; (ir.build/build-inner-fn-template) and ir.lower lowers them WITHOUT optimize-fn
25+;; (lower.lg template-value); here they get optimize-fn + structurize like a top-level
26+;; unit, since a wasm backend would have to emit them as functions too.
27+;; gotos = number of [:goto b] nodes in the structurize tree (unstructured regions);
28+;; fallbacks - gotos = loops with more than one exit (:multi).
29+;; data-types = same breakdown restricted to value-producing insts (block-arg,
30+;; branch, branch-if, return, push-closed excluded); arith = "typed/total" over
31+;; the arithmetic+comparison ops, the slice that can run unboxed.
32+;; (types = every distinct ir/type-of value with its count, "t=n;t=n", so the
33+;; :other column can be broken down; :invalid tombstones are excluded everywhere)
34+;; status: ok | fallback | build-error | optimize-error | structurize-error | expand-error | timeout
35+(require 'ir.data)
36+(require 'ir.build)
37+(require 'ir.passes.pipeline)
38+(require 'ir.structurize)
39+(require 'ir.coverage)
40+
41+(def args (vec (rest (drop-while (fn [a] (not (clojure.string/ends-with? a "census.lg"))) os/args))))
42+(def corpus-dir (let [d (nth args 0)] (if (clojure.string/ends-with? d "/") d (str d "/"))))
43+(def out-path (nth args 1))
44+(def files (vec (drop 2 args)))
45+(def unit-timeout-ms 10000)
46+
47+;; ---- file loading, copied from scripts/ir-stress.lg -------------------------
48+
49+(defn read-all [path]
50+ (try (read-code-string (str "(do " (slurp path) "\n)"))
51+ (catch e nil)))
52+
53+(defn ns-form-of [parsed]
54+ (first (filter (fn [f] (and (seq? f) (= (first f) 'ns))) (rest parsed))))
55+
56+(defn require-deps! [ns-form-]
57+ (when ns-form-
58+ (doseq [clause (drop 2 ns-form-)]
59+ (when (and (seq? clause) (= (first clause) :require))
60+ (doseq [spec (rest clause)]
61+ (try (when (or (symbol? spec) (vector? spec)) (require spec))
62+ (catch e nil)))))))
63+
64+(defn require-top-level! [parsed]
65+ (doseq [f (rest parsed)]
66+ (when (and (seq? f) (symbol? (first f))
67+ (let [h (str (first f))] (or (= h "require") (= h "use"))))
68+ (try (eval f) (catch e nil)))))
69+
70+;; ---- per-unit pipeline --------------------------------------------------------
71+
72+(defn msg-head [e]
73+ (let [m (clojure.string/replace (str e) #"[\t\n]" " ")]
74+ (subs m 0 (min 100 (count m)))))
75+
76+(defn live-values [f]
77+ ;; Values a backend would emit: block params + insts + terminator of every
78+ ;; block. DCE'd insts stay in :insts but leave the blocks, so walk blocks.
79+ (vec (for [b (ir/blocks f)
80+ v (concat (ir/block-params b f) (ir/block-insts b f) [(ir/block-term b f)])
81+ ;; DCE tombstones a dead block-param as :invalid but leaves it in
82+ ;; :params (see ir.passes.cleanup); a backend emits nothing for it.
83+ :when (and (some? v) (not= :invalid (ir/op v f)))]
84+ v)))
85+
86+(defn describe [f]
87+ (let [vals (live-values f)
88+ ops (frequencies (map (fn [v] (ir/op v f)) vals))
89+ all-tys (frequencies (map (fn [v] (str (ir/type-of v f))) vals))
90+ structural #{:block-arg :branch :branch-if :return :push-closed}
91+ arith-ops #{:add :sub :mul :quot :div :inc :dec :lt :lte :gt :gte :eq
92+ :bit-and :bit-or :bit-xor :bit-and-not :bit-not :bit-shift-left
93+ :bit-shift-right :unsigned-bit-shift-right
94+ :unchecked-add :unchecked-sub :unchecked-mul}
95+ data-vals (remove (fn [v] (contains? structural (ir/op v f))) vals)
96+ data-tys (frequencies (map (fn [v] (str (ir/type-of v f))) data-vals))
97+ arith-vals (filter (fn [v] (contains? arith-ops (ir/op v f))) vals)
98+ arith-typed (count (filter (fn [v] (contains? #{:int :float :bool} (ir/type-of v f))) arith-vals))
99+ tys (frequencies (map (fn [v] (let [t (ir/type-of v f)]
100+ (if (contains? #{:int :float :bool :unknown} t) t :other)))
101+ vals))
102+ flag-ops [:make-closure :try :dot :set-var :tail-call :recur-fn :def :load-closed]]
103+ {:nvals (count vals)
104+ :types tys
105+ :all-types all-tys
106+ :data-types data-tys
107+ :arith (str arith-typed "/" (count arith-vals))
108+ :flags (vec (filter (fn [k] (pos? (get ops k 0))) flag-ops))
109+ :ops ops}))
110+
111+(defn count-gotos [tree]
112+ (count (filter (fn [n] (and (vector? n) (= :goto (first n)))) (tree-seq vector? seq tree))))
113+
114+(defn structurize-result [f]
115+ (let [s (try (ir.structurize/structurize f)
116+ (catch e {:status :structurize-error :msg (msg-head e) :e e}))]
117+ (cond (:status s) s
118+ (pos? (:fallbacks s)) {:status :fallback :fallbacks (:fallbacks s) :gotos (count-gotos (:tree s))}
119+ :else {:status :ok :fallbacks 0 :gotos 0})))
120+
121+(defn inner-templates [f]
122+ ;; Nested fn* bodies: :const insts whose aux is {:kind :fn-template :fn <Function>}
123+ ;; or {:kind :multi-fn-template :fns [...]} (see ir.lower/template-value).
124+ (vec (for [v (live-values f)
125+ :when (= :const (ir/op v f))
126+ :let [aux (ir/aux v f)]
127+ :when (and (map? aux) (contains? #{:fn-template :multi-fn-template} (:kind aux)))
128+ t (if (= :fn-template (:kind aux)) [aux] (:fns aux))
129+ :when (:fn t)]
130+ (:fn t))))
131+
132+(defn run-inner [f]
133+ (let [opt (try (do (ir.passes.pipeline/optimize-fn f) nil)
134+ (catch e {:status :optimize-error :msg (msg-head e) :e e}))
135+ d (assoc (describe f) :f f)]
136+ (if opt (merge opt d) (merge d (structurize-result f)))))
137+
138+(defn run-unit [name args-vec body]
139+ (let [expanded (try (apply list 'defn name args-vec (map ir.passes.pipeline/expand-all body))
140+ (catch e {:status :expand-error :msg (msg-head e) :e e}))]
141+ (if (map? expanded)
142+ expanded
143+ (let [f (try (ir.build/build-fn expanded)
144+ (catch e {:status :build-error :msg (msg-head e) :e e}))]
145+ (if (map? f)
146+ f
147+ (run-inner f))))))
148+
149+(defn with-timeout [thunk ms]
150+ (let [fut (future* thunk)
151+ deadline (+ (System/nanoTime) (* ms 1000000))]
152+ (loop []
153+ (cond (realized? fut) (try (deref fut) (catch e {:status :build-error :msg (msg-head e) :e e}))
154+ (> (System/nanoTime) deadline) {:status :timeout :msg "timeout"}
155+ :else (do (sleep 5) (recur))))))
156+
157+(defn arity-units [form]
158+ ;; -> [[arity-label args-vec body] ...]; mirrors compile-form*'s single/multi split.
159+ (let [maybe-doc (nth form 2)
160+ has-doc? (string? maybe-doc)
161+ first-form (if has-doc? (nth form 3) maybe-doc)]
162+ (if (or (vector? first-form) (ir.build/return-hinted-arity-vector? first-form))
163+ [["1" first-form (drop (if has-doc? 4 3) form)]]
164+ (vec (map-indexed (fn [i a] [(str "m" i) (first a) (rest a)])
165+ (drop (if has-doc? 3 2) form))))))
166+
167+(def rows (atom []))
168+(def tally (atom {}))
169+
170+(defn record! [file nm arity r]
171+ (let [bucket (if (:e r) (str (ir.coverage/classify-error (:e r))) "")
172+ tys (or (:types r) {})
173+ ops (or (:ops r) {})]
174+ (swap! tally update (:status r) (fnil inc 0))
175+ (swap! rows conj
176+ (clojure.string/join "\t"
177+ [file (str nm) arity (name (:status r)) bucket (or (:msg r) "")
178+ (str (or (:fallbacks r) 0)) (str (or (:nvals r) 0))
179+ (str (get tys :int 0)) (str (get tys :float 0)) (str (get tys :bool 0))
180+ (str (get tys :unknown 0)) (str (get tys :other 0))
181+ (clojure.string/join "," (map (fn [k] (subs (str k) 1)) (or (:flags r) [])))
182+ (clojure.string/join ";" (map (fn [[k v]] (str (subs (str k) 1) "=" v)) (sort-by (fn [[k _]] (str k)) ops)))
183+ (clojure.string/join ";" (map (fn [[k v]] (str k "=" v)) (sort-by (fn [[k _]] k) (or (:all-types r) {}))))
184+ (clojure.string/join ";" (map (fn [[k v]] (str k "=" v)) (sort-by (fn [[k _]] k) (or (:data-types r) {}))))
185+ (or (:arith r) "0/0")
186+ (str (or (:gotos r) 0))]))))
187+
188+(defn census-file [rel]
189+ (let [path (str corpus-dir rel)
190+ parsed (read-all path)]
191+ (if (nil? parsed)
192+ (do (println (str "READ-ERROR " rel))
193+ (swap! tally update :read-error (fnil inc 0)))
194+ (let [nsf (ns-form-of parsed)
195+ ns-sym (when nsf (nth nsf 1))]
196+ (when ns-sym (try (eval (list 'in-ns (list 'quote ns-sym))) (catch e nil)))
197+ (require-deps! nsf)
198+ (require-top-level! parsed)
199+ (let [{units :fixtures names :defined-names} (ir.passes.pipeline/analyze-ns-forms (rest parsed))]
200+ (when-let [decl (seq (remove (fn [nm] (some? (resolve nm))) names))]
201+ (try (eval (cons 'declare decl)) (catch e nil)))
202+ (doseq [u units
203+ [arity args-vec body] (arity-units u)]
204+ (let [name (nth u 1)
205+ r (with-timeout (fn [] (run-unit name args-vec body)) unit-timeout-ms)]
206+ (record! rel name arity r)
207+ (loop [todo (vec (map-indexed (fn [i t] [(str "inner:" arity "/" i) t])
208+ (if (:f r) (inner-templates (:f r)) [])))]
209+ (when (seq todo)
210+ (let [[label t] (peek todo)
211+ ir (with-timeout (fn [] (run-inner t)) unit-timeout-ms)]
212+ (record! rel name label ir)
213+ (recur (into (pop todo)
214+ (map-indexed (fn [i t2] [(str label "." i) t2])
215+ (if (:f ir) (inner-templates (:f ir)) [])))))))))
216+ (println (str rel ": " (count units) " units")))))))
217+
218+(defn run []
219+ ;; Pre-load every file's deps + names first so cross-file refs resolve.
220+ (doseq [rel files]
221+ (try (let [parsed (read-all (str corpus-dir rel))
222+ nsf (ns-form-of parsed)]
223+ (when nsf (eval (list 'in-ns (list 'quote (nth nsf 1)))))
224+ (require-deps! nsf)
225+ (require-top-level! parsed))
226+ (catch e nil)))
227+ (doseq [rel files] (census-file rel))
228+ (spit out-path (str (clojure.string/join "\n" @rows) "\n"))
229+ (println "status tally:" @tally)
230+ (println "rows:" (count @rows) "->" out-path))
231+
232+(run)

dev/emit-wasm-probe/census/probe-dump.lg

+27 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
1+;; probe-dump.lg — dump one defn's optimized IR and its structurize tree.
2+;; LG_SOURCE_PATHS=<root> lg probe-dump.lg <root> <file-rel> <defn-name>
3+;; Loads the file the way census.lg does (in-ns + requires, nothing evaluated),
4+;; picks the named unit from analyze-ns-forms, and prints ir.dump + the tree.
5+(require 'ir.data) (require 'ir.build) (require 'ir.dump) (require 'ir.passes.pipeline) (require 'ir.structurize)
6+(def args (vec (rest (drop-while (fn [a] (not (clojure.string/ends-with? a "probe-dump.lg"))) os/args))))
7+(defn run []
8+ (let [root (nth args 0) rel (nth args 1) nm (symbol (nth args 2))
9+ parsed (read-code-string (str "(do " (slurp (str root "/" rel)) "\n)"))
10+ nsf (first (filter (fn [f] (and (seq? f) (= (first f) 'ns))) (rest parsed)))]
11+ (when nsf
12+ (eval (list 'in-ns (list 'quote (nth nsf 1))))
13+ (doseq [c (drop 2 nsf) :when (and (seq? c) (= :require (first c))) spec (rest c)]
14+ (try (require spec) (catch e nil))))
15+ (let [{units :fixtures names :defined-names} (ir.passes.pipeline/analyze-ns-forms (rest parsed))
16+ _ (when-let [d (seq (remove (fn [n] (some? (resolve n))) names))] (try (eval (cons 'declare d)) (catch e nil)))
17+ u (first (filter (fn [u] (= (nth u 1) nm)) units))
18+ doc? (string? (nth u 2))
19+ argv (if doc? (nth u 3) (nth u 2))
20+ body (drop (if doc? 4 3) u)
21+ f (ir.build/build-fn (apply list 'defn nm argv (map ir.passes.pipeline/expand-all body)))]
22+ (ir.passes.pipeline/optimize-fn f)
23+ (let [d (ir.dump/dump f)] (when (string? d) (println d)))
24+ (let [{:keys [tree fallbacks]} (ir.structurize/structurize f)]
25+ (println "fallbacks:" fallbacks)
26+ (println "tree:" (pr-str tree))))))
27+(run)
python

1+#!/usr/bin/env python3
2+"""Summarise the coverage runs for one corpus as markdown.
3+
4+ uv run python summarize.py <corpus-name> <stress-lower.tsv> [<stress-lower-go.tsv>] <census.tsv>
5+
6+Reads the ir-stress per-defn TSVs (file, defn, bucket, ms) and census.lg's TSV,
7+collapses the volatile parts of error buckets (block ids, value ids) so like
8+failures count together, and prints the tables the report uses. Stdlib only.
9+"""
10+import collections
11+import re
12+import sys
13+
14+ALL_OPS = """Const LoadArg LoadVar LoadClosed BlockArg SetVar Call TailCall Add Sub Mul BitAnd BitOr
15+BitXor BitAndNot BitShiftLeft BitShiftRight UnsignedBitShiftRight Quot Div UncheckedAdd UncheckedSub
16+UncheckedMul Lt Lte Gt Gte Eq Inc Dec BitNot Pop Return Branch BranchIf MakeClosure PushClosed Try Dot
17+Def RecurFn""".split()
18+
19+
20+def kebab(camel):
21+ return re.sub(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])", "-", camel).lower()
22+
23+
24+OP_KEBAB = [kebab(o) for o in ALL_OPS]
25+
26+
27+def norm_bucket(b):
28+ b = re.sub(r"for block \d+ \(\d+ vs \d+\)", "for block N (a vs b)", b)
29+ b = re.sub(r"value %\d+", "value %N", b)
30+ b = re.sub(r"\(defined in block \d+, used in block \d+\)", "(defined in block X, used in block Y)", b)
31+ b = re.sub(r"\d+", "N", b) if b.startswith(":other") else b
32+ return b[:110]
33+
34+
35+def short(path):
36+ return path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] if "/test/" not in path else "test/" + path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
37+
38+
39+def stress(path, label):
40+ rows = [l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(path) if l.strip()]
41+ total = len(rows)
42+ ok = sum(1 for r in rows if r[2] == ":ok")
43+ buckets = collections.Counter()
44+ example = {}
45+ for f, d, b, ms in rows:
46+ if b == ":ok":
47+ continue
48+ nb = norm_bucket(b)
49+ buckets[nb] += 1
50+ example.setdefault(nb, f"{short(f)} {d}")
51+ is_test = lambda r: "/test/" in r[0]
52+ prog = [r for r in rows if not is_test(r)]
53+ test = [r for r in rows if is_test(r)]
54+ print(f"### ir-stress `{label}`: {ok}/{total} defns ok ({100*ok/total:.1f}%)")
55+ if test:
56+ po = sum(1 for r in prog if r[2] == ":ok")
57+ to = sum(1 for r in test if r[2] == ":ok")
58+ print(f"- program files: {po}/{len(prog)} ({100*po/len(prog):.1f}%); test files: {to}/{len(test)} ({100*to/len(test):.1f}%)")
59+ print()
60+ if buckets:
61+ print("| bucket (normalised) | n | example |")
62+ print("|---|---:|---|")
63+ for b, n in buckets.most_common(12):
64+ print(f"| `{b}` | {n} | {example[b]} |")
65+ rest = sum(buckets.values()) - sum(n for _, n in buckets.most_common(12))
66+ if rest:
67+ print(f"| (other) | {rest} | |")
68+ print()
69+
70+
71+def census(path):
72+ cols = "file name arity status bucket msg fallbacks nvals int float bool unknown other flags ops types data_types arith gotos".split()
73+ allrows = [dict(zip(cols, l.rstrip("\n").split("\t"))) for l in open(path) if l.strip()]
74+ inner = [r for r in allrows if r["arity"].startswith("inner")]
75+ rows = [r for r in allrows if not r["arity"].startswith("inner")]
76+ units = len(rows)
77+ st = collections.Counter(r["status"] for r in rows)
78+ # per-defn: ok iff every arity ok
79+ per = collections.defaultdict(list)
80+ for r in rows:
81+ per[(r["file"], r["name"])].append(r["status"])
82+ defn_ok = sum(1 for v in per.values() if all(s == "ok" for s in v))
83+ print(f"### structurize census: {st['ok']}/{units} units ok ({100*st['ok']/units:.1f}%); "
84+ f"{defn_ok}/{len(per)} defns with every arity ok ({100*defn_ok/len(per):.1f}%)")
85+ print()
86+ print("| status | units |")
87+ print("|---|---:|")
88+ for s, n in st.most_common():
89+ print(f"| {s} | {n} |")
90+ print()
91+ prog = [r for r in rows if "/test/" not in r["file"]]
92+ if len(prog) != len(rows):
93+ po = sum(1 for r in prog if r["status"] == "ok")
94+ test = [r for r in rows if "/test/" in r["file"]]
95+ to = sum(1 for r in test if r["status"] == "ok")
96+ print(f"- program files: {po}/{len(prog)} units ok ({100*po/len(prog):.1f}%); "
97+ f"test files: {to}/{len(test)} ({100*to/len(test):.1f}%)")
98+ print()
99+ errs = collections.Counter()
100+ ex = {}
101+ for r in rows:
102+ if r["status"] in ("ok", "fallback"):
103+ continue
104+ k = (r["status"], r["bucket"], norm_bucket(r["msg"]))
105+ errs[k] += 1
106+ ex.setdefault(k, f"{short(r['file'])} {r['name']}")
107+ if errs:
108+ print("| status | classify-error | message head | n | example |")
109+ print("|---|---|---|---:|---|")
110+ for (s, b, m), n in errs.most_common(20):
111+ print(f"| {s} | `{b}` | `{m}` | {n} | {ex[(s,b,m)]} |")
112+ print()
113+ if inner:
114+ ist = collections.Counter(r["status"] for r in inner)
115+ print(f"- nested fn* bodies (inner :fn-template units, optimize-fn + structurize run here): "
116+ f"{len(inner)} units; " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in ist.most_common()))
117+ ierr = collections.Counter((r["status"], norm_bucket(r["msg"])) for r in inner if r["status"] not in ("ok", "fallback"))
118+ for (st_, m), n in ierr.most_common(8):
119+ print(f" - {st_} `{m}` x{n}")
120+ print()
121+ fb = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "fallback"]
122+ if fb:
123+ gotos = sum(int(r["gotos"]) for r in fb)
124+ fbs = sum(int(r["fallbacks"]) for r in fb)
125+ print(f"- fallback kinds: {gotos} [:goto] nodes, {fbs-gotos} multi-exit loops (:multi) across {len(fb)} units")
126+ fbc = collections.Counter(int(r["fallbacks"]) for r in fb)
127+ print(f"- fallbacks>0 units: {len(fb)}; fallback-count distribution: "
128+ + ", ".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in sorted(fbc.items())))
129+ print("- examples: " + ", ".join(f"{short(r['file'])} {r['name']}" for r in fb[:10]))
130+ print()
131+ # ops over built units
132+ built = [r for r in allrows if r["ops"]]
133+ print(f"(built units = {sum(1 for r in rows if r['ops'])} top-level + {sum(1 for r in inner if r['ops'])} inner)\n")
134+ ops = collections.Counter()
135+ fns_using = collections.Counter()
136+ for r in built:
137+ for kv in r["ops"].split(";"):
138+ k, v = kv.split("=")
139+ ops[k] += int(v)
140+ fns_using[k] += 1
141+ print(f"### IR op histogram over {len(built)} built units (live values after optimize)")
142+ print()
143+ print("| op | insts | units using it |")
144+ print("|---|---:|---:|")
145+ seen = set()
146+ for k in OP_KEBAB:
147+ seen.add(k)
148+ if ops[k]:
149+ print(f"| {k} | {ops[k]} | {fns_using[k]} |")
150+ for k, n in ops.most_common():
151+ if k not in seen:
152+ print(f"| {k} (not in the 41-op list) | {n} | {fns_using[k]} |")
153+ absent = [k for k in OP_KEBAB if not ops[k]]
154+ print()
155+ print("- ops never seen: " + ", ".join(absent))
156+ print()
157+ print("| feature | units using it | % of built |")
158+ print("|---|---:|---:|")
159+ for k in ["make-closure", "try", "dot", "set-var", "tail-call", "recur-fn", "def", "load-closed"]:
160+ print(f"| :{k} | {fns_using[k]} | {100*fns_using[k]/len(built):.1f}% |")
161+ print()
162+ tot = collections.Counter()
163+ for r in built:
164+ for k in ["int", "float", "bool", "unknown", "other"]:
165+ tot[k] += int(r[k])
166+ n = sum(tot.values())
167+ print(f"### type distribution over {n} live IR values (ir/type-of after optimize)")
168+ print()
169+ print("| type | values | % |")
170+ print("|---|---:|---:|")
171+ for k in ["int", "float", "bool", "unknown", "other"]:
172+ print(f"| :{k} | {tot[k]} | {100*tot[k]/n:.1f}% |")
173+ typed = tot["int"] + tot["float"] + tot["bool"]
174+ print(f"\n- typed (:int/:float/:bool): {typed}/{n} = {100*typed/n:.1f}%")
175+ # excluding structural values that carry no data type (block-arg/branch/return/pop)
176+ # is not possible from the aggregate, so also report units that are fully unknown
177+ all_unknown = sum(1 for r in built if int(r["int"]) + int(r["float"]) + int(r["bool"]) == 0)
178+ print(f"- units with zero typed values: {all_unknown}/{len(built)} ({100*all_unknown/len(built):.1f}%)")
179+ at = sum(int(r["arith"].split("/")[0]) for r in built)
180+ aa = sum(int(r["arith"].split("/")[1]) for r in built)
181+ print(f"- arithmetic/comparison insts typed :int/:float/:bool (run unboxed): {at}/{aa} = {100*at/max(aa,1):.1f}%")
182+ dt = collections.Counter()
183+ for r in built:
184+ for kv in (r.get("data_types") or "").split(";"):
185+ if kv:
186+ k, v = kv.rsplit("=", 1)
187+ dt[k] += int(v)
188+ dn = sum(dt.values())
189+ dtyped = dt[":int"] + dt[":float"] + dt[":bool"]
190+ print(f"- value-producing insts only (block-arg/branch/branch-if/return/push-closed excluded): {dn} values; "
191+ f":unknown {100*dt[':unknown']/dn:.1f}%, :int/:float/:bool {100*dtyped/dn:.1f}%, "
192+ f"other known types {100*(dn-dt[':unknown']-dtyped)/dn:.1f}%")
193+ print()
194+ full = collections.Counter()
195+ for r in built:
196+ for kv in (r.get("types") or "").split(";"):
197+ if not kv:
198+ continue
199+ k, v = kv.rsplit("=", 1)
200+ if k.startswith("[:const "):
201+ k = "[:const " + k.split()[1] + " ...]"
202+ full[k] += int(v)
203+ print("Full ir/type-of breakdown (the :other column above expanded):")
204+ print()
205+ print("| type | values | % |")
206+ print("|---|---:|---:|")
207+ shown = 0
208+ for k, v in full.most_common(14):
209+ print(f"| `{k}` | {v} | {100*v/n:.1f}% |")
210+ shown += v
211+ if n - shown:
212+ print(f"| (rest) | {n-shown} | {100*(n-shown)/n:.1f}% |")
213+ print()
214+
215+
216+def main():
217+ name, lower, *rest = sys.argv[1:]
218+ cen = rest[-1]
219+ print(f"## {name}\n")
220+ stress(lower, "lower")
221+ if len(rest) == 2:
222+ stress(rest[0], "lower-go")
223+ census(cen)
224+
225+
226+main()

dev/emit-wasm-probe/ext/bench-all.sh

+16 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
1+#!/bin/sh
2+# Runs each (module, kind) pair in 3 fresh node processes and prints the
3+# median of the three per-process medians and the min of the three per-process
4+# mins (REPS per process, default 5). Run from the ext/ dir after gen-ext.lg.
5+set -e
6+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
7+run3() { # run3 <wasm> <kind>
8+ out=$(for i in 1 2 3; do node bench.mjs "$1" "$2" "${REPS:-5}"; done)
9+ med=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -E 's/.*median=([0-9.]+)ms.*/\1/' | sort -n | sed -n 2p)
10+ min=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -E 's/.*min=([0-9.]+)ms.*/\1/' | sort -n | sed -n 1p)
11+ printf '%-14s %-5s median %8s ms min %8s ms\n' "$1" "$2" "$med" "$min"
12+}
13+for pair in "fib.wasm fib" "fib-chk.wasm fib" "fib-chki.wasm fib" "fib-chkt.wasm fib" "fib-try.wasm fib" "fib-i31.wasm fib" \
14+ "fibl.wasm fibl" "fibl-chk.wasm fibl" "fibl-chki.wasm fibl" "fibl-chkt.wasm fibl"; do
15+ set -- $pair; run3 "$1" "$2"
16+done

dev/emit-wasm-probe/ext/bench.mjs

+19 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
1+// Usage: node bench.mjs <module.wasm> <fib|fibl> [reps]
2+// fib = fib(32) through the boxed export + unbox; fibl = fibl(90) x 1e6.
3+// Prints the median and min of `reps` timed iterations after 3 warm-ups, in ms.
4+// Min is the robust figure on a loaded machine; median on a quiet one.
5+import fs from 'node:fs';
6+const [, , file, kind, repsArg] = process.argv;
7+const reps = Number(repsArg ?? 5);
8+const ex = (await WebAssembly.instantiate(fs.readFileSync(file))).instance.exports;
9+const bench = {
10+ fib: () => ex.unbox(ex.fib(32n)),
11+ fibl: () => { let r; for (let i = 0; i < 1e6; i++) r = ex.fibl(90n); return r; },
12+}[kind];
13+if (!bench) throw new Error('kind must be fib or fibl');
14+for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) bench();
15+const times = [];
16+let r;
17+for (let i = 0; i < reps; i++) { const t = performance.now(); r = bench(); times.push(performance.now() - t); }
18+times.sort((a, b) => a - b);
19+console.log(`${file} ${kind} result=${r} median=${times[reps >> 1].toFixed(2)}ms min=${times[0].toFixed(2)}ms all=[${times.map(t => t.toFixed(1)).join(' ')}]`);

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
1+// wasm-tools 1.256 no longer parses the legacy `try/do/catch` text form, so this
2+// hand-assembles the equivalent binary (run(x): x<0 ? 1000+x : 2x) to test whether
3+// hosts still ACCEPT legacy EH. Writes eh-legacy.wasm and tries to run it here.
4+import fs from 'node:fs';
5+const u = n => { const o = []; do { let b = n & 0x7f; n >>>= 7; if (n) b |= 0x80; o.push(b); } while (n); return o; };
6+const str = s => [...u(s.length), ...Buffer.from(s)];
7+const sec = (id, body) => [id, ...u(body.length), ...body];
8+const vec = items => [...u(items.length), ...items.flat()];
9+const I64 = 0x7e;
10+const types = vec([[0x60, 1, I64, 1, I64], [0x60, 1, I64, 0]]);
11+const funcs = vec([[0]]);
12+const tags = vec([[0x00, 1]]); // attribute 0, type 1
13+const exports_ = vec([[...str('run'), 0x00, 0]]);
14+const body = [0x00, // no locals
15+ 0x06, I64, // try (result i64) -- legacy opcode
16+ 0x20, 0, 0x42, 0, 0x53, // local.get 0; i64.const 0; i64.lt_s
17+ 0x04, 0x40, 0x20, 0, 0x08, 0, 0x0b, // if; local.get 0; throw 0; end
18+ 0x20, 0, 0x42, 2, 0x7e, // local.get 0; i64.const 2; i64.mul
19+ 0x07, 0, // catch 0 -- legacy opcode
20+ 0x42, 0xe8, 0x07, 0x7c, // i64.const 1000; i64.add
21+ 0x0b, 0x0b];
22+const code = vec([[...u(body.length), ...body]]);
23+const mod = Buffer.from([0, 0x61, 0x73, 0x6d, 1, 0, 0, 0, ...sec(1, types), ...sec(3, funcs), ...sec(13, tags), ...sec(7, exports_), ...sec(10, code)]);
24+fs.writeFileSync('eh-legacy.wasm', mod);
25+try {
26+ const ex = (await WebAssembly.instantiate(mod)).instance.exports;
27+ console.log('node legacy EH: run(5) =', ex.run(5n), ' run(-3) =', ex.run(-3n));
28+} catch (e) { console.log('node legacy EH FAILED:', e.message.split('\n')[0]); }

1+;; Variants of gen.lg for the host-capability/cost questions in ext/README.md.
2+;; Run from the probe dir: lg -source-paths . ext/gen-ext.lg
3+(require (quote lower-wasm))
4+(declare fib fibl)
5+(def fibl-src '(defn fibl [^long n] (loop [a 0 b 1 i 0] (if (< i n) (recur b (+ a b) (inc i)) a))))
6+(def fib-src '(defn fib [^long n] (if (< n 2) n (+ (fib (- n 1)) (fib (- n 2))))))
7+
8+(defn emit [path src & {:keys [checked trap box guard]}]
9+ (binding [lower-wasm/*checked* checked
10+ lower-wasm/*trap* (boolean trap)
11+ lower-wasm/*box* (or box :struct)
12+ lower-wasm/*guard-calls* (boolean guard)]
13+ (spit path (lower-wasm/module src))
14+ (println "wrote" path)))
15+
16+(emit "ext/fib.wat" fib-src) ; control (= ../fib.wat)
17+(emit "ext/fibl.wat" fibl-src)
18+(emit "ext/fib-chk.wat" fib-src :checked :call) ; Q1: helper-call checks, throw
19+(emit "ext/fibl-chk.wat" fibl-src :checked :call)
20+(emit "ext/fib-chki.wat" fib-src :checked :inline) ; Q1: inline checks, throw
21+(emit "ext/fibl-chki.wat" fibl-src :checked :inline)
22+(emit "ext/fib-chkt.wat" fib-src :checked :inline :trap true) ; Q1: inline checks, unreachable
23+(emit "ext/fibl-chkt.wat" fibl-src :checked :inline :trap true)
24+(emit "ext/fib-try.wat" fib-src :guard true) ; Q3: try_table around self-calls
25+(emit "ext/fib-i31.wat" fib-src :box :i31) ; Q5: i31ref boxing

1+// Q4: WebAssembly.Suspending + WebAssembly.promising in Node (no flags).
2+import fs from 'node:fs';
3+console.log('Suspending' in WebAssembly ? 'JSPI API present' : 'NO JSPI API', `(node ${process.version}, v8 ${process.versions.v8})`);
4+let sleeps = 0;
5+const sleep = new WebAssembly.Suspending(ms => { sleeps++; return new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms)); });
6+const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiate(fs.readFileSync('jspi.wasm'), { env: { sleep } });
7+const run = WebAssembly.promising(instance.exports.run);
8+const loopSum = WebAssembly.promising(instance.exports.loop_sum);
9+let t = performance.now();
10+const p = run(5n);
11+console.log('run(5) returned', p.constructor.name, 'synchronously;', 'sleeps so far:', sleeps);
12+console.log('run(5) =', await p, '(expect 156) after', (performance.now() - t).toFixed(1), 'ms (sleep was 5 ms)');
13+t = performance.now();
14+const [a, b] = await Promise.all([run(1n), loopSum(10)]); // two suspended stacks interleaved
15+console.log('run(1) =', a, '(expect 112); loop_sum(10) =', b, '(expect 45) after', (performance.now() - t).toFixed(1), 'ms; total sleeps:', sleeps);
16+try { instance.exports.run(5n); console.log('unwrapped export call: no error'); }
17+catch (e) { console.log('unwrapped export call (no promising):', e.constructor.name, '-', e.message); }

1+// Builds wasmtime-bench.wat: fib + fibl from the generated WAT, plus WASI-timed
2+// bench exports so `wasmtime run --invoke bench_fib wasmtime-bench.wasm` prints
3+// elapsed nanoseconds (no i64-arg passing or GC-ref printing needed).
4+// Usage: node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs [fib.wat fibl.wat out.wat] (defaults shown)
5+import fs from 'node:fs';
6+const [FIB = 'fib.wat', FIBL = 'fibl.wat', OUT = 'wasmtime-bench.wat'] = process.argv.slice(2);
7+const fnOf = (file, name) => {
8+ const wat = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
9+ const i = wat.indexOf('(func $self');
10+ return wat.slice(i, wat.lastIndexOf(')')).replace('$self', name).replace(/ \(export "[a-z]+"\)/, '').replaceAll('call $self', 'call ' + name);
11+};
12+const runtime = (() => { const w = fs.readFileSync(FIB, 'utf8'); return w.slice(w.indexOf('\n') + 1, w.indexOf('(func $self')); })();
13+fs.writeFileSync(OUT, `(module
14+(import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "clock_time_get" (func $clock (param i32 i64 i32) (result i32)))
15+(memory (export "memory") 1)
16+(func $now (result i64) (drop (call $clock (i32.const 1) (i64.const 1) (i32.const 8))) (i64.load (i32.const 8)))
17+${runtime.replace('(func (export "unbox")', '(func $unbox')}
18+${fnOf(FIB, '$fib')}
19+${fnOf(FIBL, '$fibl')}
20+(func (export "fib32") (result i64) (call $unbox (call $fib (i64.const 32))))
21+(func (export "bench_fib") (result i64) (local $t i64) (local $i i32)
22+ (loop $w (drop (call $fib (i64.const 32))) (local.set $i (i32.add (local.get $i) (i32.const 1))) (br_if $w (i32.lt_u (local.get $i) (i32.const 3))))
23+ (local.set $t (call $now))
24+ (drop (call $fib (i64.const 32)))
25+ (i64.sub (call $now) (local.get $t)))
26+(func (export "bench_fibl") (result i64) (local $t i64) (local $i i32) (local $r i64)
27+ (local.set $t (call $now))
28+ (loop $l (local.set $r (call $fibl (i64.const 90))) (local.set $i (i32.add (local.get $i) (i32.const 1))) (br_if $l (i32.lt_u (local.get $i) (i32.const 1000000))))
29+ (if (i64.ne (local.get $r) (i64.const 2880067194370816120)) (then unreachable))
30+ (i64.sub (call $now) (local.get $t)))
31+)
32+`);

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/affected.sh [--all] [<path>...] — which items.tsv rows a change touches.
3+#
4+# With no args: paths = `git diff --name-only HEAD` (staged and unstaged) +
5+# untracked files under dev/lower-wasm (what an implementer is about to hand
6+# over). Runs under macOS bash 3.2; advisory only (D106), gates stay full. With paths:
7+# those. Prints the item ids whose check reads at least one of the paths,
8+# one per line, in items.tsv order; --all prints the id → inputs table.
9+#
10+# The map is a static table (below), not derived: every check script names
11+# its inputs in its header, and the table is the one place that has to move
12+# when a check grows a new input. Tokens are dir prefixes under dev/lower-wasm
13+# (`src/` = the backend, `rt/` = the runtime, `corpus/<x>/` = that corpus,
14+# `checks/<name>` = the script itself, `host/`), plus `xsofy`/`legmacs`
15+# for the external corpora (census, world-parity, native-twins).
16+#
17+# Rule of thumb the table encodes (measured 2026-10-01, perf-report.md):
18+# src/ change -> every oracle row + census (30 min fresh) + bench-fib
19+# rt/ change -> oracle rows that run programs (the runtime is linked in),
20+# native tier, review2, twins; NOT census, NOT refuse,
21+# NOT bench-fib (fib reaches no runtime: 1.3 KB shaken)
22+# corpus/x/ only -> the rows that read corpus/x (no rtlib rebuild happens
23+# either way: the key hashes rt/ + src/ only)
24+# checks/ only -> the rows whose command names that script
25+set -uo pipefail
26+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
27+# id<TAB>space-separated input prefixes. "oracle" expands to the compile+run
28+# path: src/ rt/ checks/oracle.sh checks/wasm-run.sh src/run.mjs.
29+table() { cat <<'EOF'
30+P0.1 checks/run-corpus.sh checks/sem.sh checks/gate.sh checks/census.sh checks/census.lg checks/census-summary.py checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh checks/intrinsics-native-runner.lg checks/run.sh corpus/scalar/
31+P1.0 oracle corpus/scalar/
32+P1.1 oracle corpus/scalar/ corpus/opmatrix/ corpus/typed/ checks/run-corpus.sh
33+P1.2 oracle corpus/control/ checks/run-corpus.sh
34+P1.3 oracle corpus/closure/ checks/run-corpus.sh
35+P1.4 src/ checks/wasm-run.sh checks/refuse.sh corpus/refused/
36+P1.5 src/ checks/census.sh checks/census.lg checks/census-summary.py xsofy legmacs
37+P1.6 src/ checks/census.sh checks/census.lg checks/census-summary.py xsofy legmacs oracle corpus/census/switch/
38+P1.7 oracle corpus/review/ checks/run-corpus.sh checks/refuse.sh
39+P1.GATE src/ checks/bench-fib.sh checks/bench-fib.mjs checks/bench-fib-probe.lg corpus/scalar/fib.clj
40+P2.1 oracle corpus/wasm/ checks/run-corpus.sh
41+P2.2 oracle corpus/hash/ checks/hash-parity.sh checks/wasm-hash.sh
42+P2.3 oracle corpus/core-tests.txt checks/run-tests.sh checks/run-tests.skip src/testshim.lg
43+P2.4 oracle corpus/maporder/ checks/map-order.sh checks/run-tests.sh
44+P2.5 oracle corpus/seqs/ checks/run-corpus.sh
45+P2.6 oracle corpus/core-tests.txt checks/run-tests.sh
46+P2.7 oracle checks/run-roundtrip.sh
47+P2.9 rt/ corpus/intrinsics/ checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh checks/intrinsics-native-runner.lg
48+P2.8 rt/ corpus/natives/ checks/native-twins.sh tools/
49+P2.10 rt/ corpus/review2/ checks/run-review2.sh
50+P2.11 oracle corpus/wasm/ checks/run-corpus.sh
51+P2.12 oracle corpus/wasm/pending/variadic/ corpus/refused/ checks/refuse.sh
52+P3.0 rt/ corpus/intrinsics/ corpus/edn/ checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh
53+P3.1 rt/ corpus/natives/ checks/native-twins.sh tools/
54+P3.2 oracle corpus/dump-world.lg checks/world-parity.sh xsofy
55+P4.0 oracle host/ corpus/host/ checks/browser-boot.sh checks/browser-boot.mjs
56+P4.1 oracle host/ corpus/host/ checks/browser-boot.sh checks/browser-boot.mjs xsofy
57+P4.2 oracle host/ checks/lane5.sh xsofy
58+P4.3 oracle host/ checks/size-boot.sh xsofy
59+EOF
60+}
61+# BSD sed has no \b: the token is always first in column 2, so match it there.
62+expand() { awk -F'\t' 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {sub(/^oracle /, "src/ rt/ checks/oracle.sh checks/wasm-run.sh ", $2); print}'; }
63+if [ "${1:-}" = --all ]; then table | expand; exit 0; fi
64+# bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash) has no mapfile. --relative keeps paths relative to
65+# this dir wherever the checkout sits (a worktree, a copy inside another repo);
66+# --no-renames lists both ends of a rename; `diff HEAD` covers staged and
67+# unstaged tracked changes, ls-files --others the new untracked files.
68+paths=()
69+if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then paths=("$@"); else
70+ git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "affected.sh: not in a git checkout; pass paths explicitly" >&2; exit 2; }
71+ while IFS= read -r p; do [ -n "$p" ] && paths+=("$p"); done < <({ git diff --name-only --relative --no-renames HEAD -- . ; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . ; } | sort -u)
72+fi
73+[ ${#paths[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "no changes" >&2; exit 0; }
74+# a path matches a token when the token is a prefix of it (dirs end in /),
75+# or equals it; the external corpora match on their checkout paths.
76+table | expand | while IFS=$'\t' read -r id inputs; do
77+ hit=0
78+ for tok in $inputs; do
79+ for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
80+ case $p in "$tok"*) hit=1 ;; esac
81+ case $tok in xsofy|legmacs) case $p in *"/3p/$tok/"*) hit=1 ;; esac ;; esac
82+ [ $hit = 1 ] && break 2
83+ done
84+ done
85+ [ $hit = 1 ] && echo "$id"
86+done

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
1+// node checks/bench-fib.mjs <backend.wasm> <probe.wasm> [reps]
2+// fib(32) through each module's exported fib(i64) in ONE process, as
3+// ../emit-wasm-probe/ext/bench.mjs times it: 3 warm-ups each, then `reps`
4+// timed runs (interleaved backend/probe so drift hits both), median per module.
5+import fs from 'node:fs';
6+const [, , backendFile, probeFile, repsArg] = process.argv;
7+const reps = Number(repsArg ?? 5);
8+const nop = () => {};
9+const load = async (f) => (await WebAssembly.instantiate(fs.readFileSync(f),
10+ { env: { print_i64: nop, print_str: nop, print_nl: nop } })).instance.exports;
11+const mods = { backend: await load(backendFile), probe: await load(probeFile) };
12+const run = (ex) => ex.fib(32n);
13+for (const ex of Object.values(mods)) for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) run(ex);
14+const times = { backend: [], probe: [] };
15+const result = {};
16+for (let i = 0; i < reps; i++) {
17+ for (const [k, ex] of Object.entries(mods)) {
18+ const t = performance.now(); result[k] = run(ex); times[k].push(performance.now() - t);
19+ }
20+}
21+const med = (a) => [...a].sort((x, y) => x - y)[a.length >> 1];
22+for (const k of Object.keys(mods)) {
23+ if (Number(result[k]) !== 2178309) { console.log(`${k}: wrong result ${result[k]}`); process.exit(1); }
24+ console.log(`${k.padEnd(8)} fib(32)=${result[k]} median=${med(times[k]).toFixed(2)}ms all=[${times[k].map((t) => t.toFixed(1)).join(' ')}]`);
25+}
26+const ratio = med(times.backend) / med(times.probe);
27+console.log(`ratio backend/probe = ${ratio.toFixed(3)} (limit 1.5)`);
28+process.exit(ratio <= 1.5 ? 0 : 1);

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/bench-fib.sh — P1.GATE perf bar: fib(32) compiled by the backend from
3+# corpus/scalar/fib.clj (checked arithmetic, hybrid boxing, as shipped) must
4+# run within 1.5x of the probe's fib-i31 variant (unchecked, i31 boxing,
5+# ^long-hinted source; ../emit-wasm-probe/ext/gen-ext.lg), both built fresh
6+# and timed in one node process. Exits 0 iff backend/probe <= 1.5.
7+# Env: LG, REPS (default 5).
8+set -uo pipefail
9+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
10+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
11+t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
12+"$LG" -source-paths "$here/src" "$here/src/driver.lg" "$here/corpus/scalar/fib.clj" "$t/backend.wat" >"$t/drv.log" 2>&1 \
13+ || { cat "$t/drv.log"; exit 1; }
14+"$LG" -source-paths "$here/../emit-wasm-probe" "$here/checks/bench-fib-probe.lg" "$t/probe.wat" >"$t/probe.log" 2>&1 \
15+ || { cat "$t/probe.log"; exit 1; }
16+wasm-tools parse "$t/backend.wat" -o "$t/backend.wasm" || exit 1
17+wasm-tools parse "$t/probe.wat" -o "$t/probe.wasm" || exit 1
18+node "$here/checks/bench-fib.mjs" "$t/backend.wasm" "$t/probe.wasm" "${REPS:-5}"

211+// ---- --xsofy -----------------------------------------------------------------
212+// The emitted xsofy module (module.wasm, the adapter's default) in the real
213+// shell, booted the way local-scripts/browser-smoke-playwright/
214+// zz-boot-time-probe.mjs boots the four let-go lanes: page load to "press any
215+// key" in the page text (the title card) = time-to-title; Space; then "hp" or
216+// "floor" in the page text (the map screen's HUD) = time-to-map, both from
217+// navigation. Also asserts what only the D100 imports can make true: the
218+// title card prints the ?seed= the page was opened with (js/url-param), and
219+// the shell received xsofy/startup with a title and xsofy/stats (js/emit).
220+async function xsofyGame(base, seed = '424242') {
221+ const browser = await chromium.launch();
222+ const out = { label: 'xsofy', seed };
223+ const page = await browser.newPage();
224+ const errors = [], bad = [];
225+ page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(String(e)));
226+ page.on('response', (r) => { if (r.status() >= 400 && !r.url().endsWith('/build-info.json')) bad.push(`${r.status()} ${r.url()}`); });
227+ page.on('console', (m) => { if (m.type() === 'error' && !/Failed to load resource/.test(m.text())) errors.push(m.text()); });
228+ await page.addInitScript(() => {
229+ window.__events = [];
230+ for (const n of ['xsofy/startup', 'xsofy/stats']) {
231+ window.addEventListener(n, (e) => window.__events.push([n, e.detail]));
232+ }
233+ });
234+ try {
235+ const t0 = Date.now();
236+ await page.goto(`${base}/index.html?seed=${seed}`, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
237+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /press any key/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
238+ out.titleMs = Date.now() - t0;
239+ out.titleSeed = await page.evaluate((s) => document.body.innerText.includes(`seed ${s}`), seed);
240+ await page.keyboard.press('Space');
241+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /hp[: ]/i.test(document.body.innerText) || /floor/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
242+ out.mapMs = Date.now() - t0;
243+ await page.waitForTimeout(500);
244+ const r = await page.evaluate(() => ({ lgw: window.__lgw, events: window.__events }));
245+ const startup = r.events.find(([n]) => n === 'xsofy/startup');
246+ out.startup = startup ? startup[1] : null;
247+ out.stats = r.events.filter(([n]) => n === 'xsofy/stats').length;
248+ out.readyMode = r.lgw.readyMode; out.coi = r.lgw.coi; out.jspi = r.lgw.jspi;
249+ out.running = !r.lgw.done;
250+ out.error = r.lgw.error || null;
251+ out.errors = errors; out.bad = bad;
252+ out.pass = out.titleSeed && !!(out.startup && out.startup.title) && out.stats > 0
253+ && out.running && !errors.length && !bad.length;
254+ } catch (e) {
255+ out.failure = String((e && e.message) || e).split('\n')[0];
256+ out.pass = false;
257+ try { out.text = (await page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText)).slice(-600); out.lgw = await page.evaluate(() => window.__lgw); } catch {}
258+ }
259+ await browser.close();
260+ return out;
261+}
262+
263+// ---- --walk -------------------------------------------------------------------
264+// Lane 5's held-key walk. Boots like zz-determinism-probe.mjs (?seed=, title,
265+// Space, map, 3 s settle), then sends auto-repeat BURSTS: n keydowns of one
266+// key dispatched in a single task on xterm's textarea (what a held key does),
267+// each burst followed by a pause long enough for the turn to resolve. let-go's
268+// key ring coalesces a burst the game has not yet read into ONE read
269+// (keysource_js_wasm.go:96-122, D98), so the dump only matches across lanes
270+// if the emitted lane's host coalesces the same way. Bursts stay under the
271+// ring's 8 slots so neither lane drops keys. Writes document.body.innerText.
272+async function heldWalk(base, seed, outFile) {
273+ const browser = await chromium.launch();
274+ const page = await browser.newPage();
275+ const out = { label: 'walk', seed };
276+ try {
277+ await page.goto(`${base}/?seed=${seed}`, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
278+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /press any key/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
279+ await page.keyboard.press('Space');
280+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /hp[: ]/i.test(document.body.innerText) || /floor/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
281+ await page.waitForTimeout(3000);
282+ const bursts = [['l', 5], ['j', 4], ['h', 6], ['k', 3], ['l', 6], ['j', 5]];
283+ for (const [key, n] of bursts) {
284+ await page.evaluate(([key, n]) => {
285+ const ta = document.querySelector('.xterm-helper-textarea');
286+ const code = 'Key' + key.toUpperCase();
287+ for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
288+ ta.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key, code, keyCode: key.toUpperCase().charCodeAt(0), repeat: i > 0, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));
289+ }
290+ }, [key, n]);
291+ await page.waitForTimeout(1200);
292+ }
293+ await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
294+ const txt = await page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText);
295+ fs.writeFileSync(outFile, txt);
296+ out.bytes = txt.length; out.bursts = bursts.map(([k, n]) => k + 'x' + n).join(' ');
297+ } catch (e) {
298+ out.failure = String((e && e.message) || e).split('\n')[0];
299+ }
300+ await browser.close();
301+ return out;
302+}
303+
304+// ---- --settle-walk -------------------------------------------------------------
305+// Lane 5's gating walk. zz-determinism-probe.mjs sends l l j j h k l j one key
306+// per 400 ms; on a loaded machine whether a key lands mid-turn or between turns
307+// varies per run, and both lanes coalesce identical queued keys (let-go's ring,
308+// D98, and the host that mirrors it), so the dump flipped between runs. Here a
309+// key is sent only once the game has finished the previous one, from two signals
310+// the game itself produces:
311+// ack the shell's `xsofy/stats` event count rose (the game read the key and
312+// resolved its turn: ui_bridge/emit-stats runs once per turn); the
313+// event's `turn` is logged so a coalesced key (turn +0) is visible;
314+// settle the xterm rows' text is unchanged for LW_SETTLE (default 3) samples
315+// 100 ms apart AND at least LW_MIN_MS (default 200) have passed since
316+// the key: emit-stats fires BEFORE the dirty render and the between-
317+// turn vfx (play/play-advance), so the ack alone would land mid-turn.
318+// Each wait is capped at 5 s; a timeout is a HARNESS failure (exit 2, `failure`),
319+// never a lane mismatch. LW_SETTLE=0 drops the quiet window and the minimum
320+// (ack only): the falsification, it lets the next key land during the vfx.
321+// Same boot and dump as the probe (?seed=, title, Space, map, 3 s, ..., body text);
322+// the per-key log (ack/settle ms, turn before/after, xterm rows) goes to
323+// <out>.steps.json so lane5.sh can show the first key at which two lanes part.
324+async function settleWalk(base, seed, outFile) {
325+ const SETTLE = parseInt(process.env.LW_SETTLE ?? '3', 10);
326+ const MIN_MS = SETTLE === 0 ? 0 : parseInt(process.env.LW_MIN_MS ?? '200', 10);
327+ const CAP_MS = 5000, POLL_MS = 100;
328+ const browser = await chromium.launch();
329+ const page = await browser.newPage();
330+ const out = { label: 'settle-walk', seed, settle: SETTLE, minMs: MIN_MS };
331+ const steps = [];
332+ await page.addInitScript(() => {
333+ window.__stats = { n: 0, turn: null };
334+ window.addEventListener('xsofy/stats', (e) => { window.__stats.n++; window.__stats.turn = e.detail && e.detail.turn; });
335+ });
336+ const rows = () => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.xterm-rows > div')].map((d) => d.textContent).join('\n'));
337+ const stats = () => page.evaluate(() => ({ ...window.__stats }));
338+ const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
339+ // returns ms until `rows` held steady for SETTLE samples and MIN_MS passed
340+ async function settle(t0) {
341+ let prev = await rows(), same = 0;
342+ for (;;) {
343+ await sleep(POLL_MS);
344+ const cur = await rows();
345+ same = cur === prev ? same + 1 : 0; prev = cur;
346+ if (same >= SETTLE && Date.now() - t0 >= MIN_MS) return Date.now() - t0;
347+ if (Date.now() - t0 > CAP_MS) throw new Error(`settle timeout (${CAP_MS} ms) after key ${steps.length}`);
348+ }
349+ }
350+ try {
351+ await page.goto(`${base}/?seed=${seed}`, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });
352+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /press any key/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
353+ await page.keyboard.press('Space');
354+ await page.waitForFunction(() => /hp[: ]/i.test(document.body.innerText) || /floor/i.test(document.body.innerText), null, { timeout: 120000 });
355+ await page.waitForTimeout(3000); // as the probe: mapgen/title-exit animation
356+ await settle(Date.now());
357+ for (const key of ['l', 'l', 'j', 'j', 'h', 'k', 'l', 'j']) {
358+ const before = await stats();
359+ const t0 = Date.now();
360+ await page.keyboard.press(key);
361+ let after;
362+ for (;;) {
363+ after = await stats();
364+ if (after.n > before.n) break;
365+ if (Date.now() - t0 > CAP_MS) throw new Error(`no xsofy/stats within ${CAP_MS} ms of key ${steps.length} ('${key}')`);
366+ await sleep(20);
367+ }
368+ const ackMs = Date.now() - t0;
369+ const settleMs = await settle(t0);
370+ const fin = await stats();
371+ steps.push({ key, turnBefore: before.turn, turnAfter: fin.turn, events: fin.n - before.n, ackMs, settleMs, rows: await rows() });
372+ }
373+ const txt = await page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText);
374+ fs.writeFileSync(outFile, txt);
375+ out.bytes = txt.length;
376+ out.turns = steps.map((s) => `${s.key}:${s.turnBefore}>${s.turnAfter}`).join(' ');
377+ out.ackMs = steps.map((s) => s.ackMs); out.settleMs = steps.map((s) => s.settleMs);
378+ } catch (e) {
379+ out.failure = String((e && e.message) || e).split('\n')[0];
380+ }
381+ try { fs.writeFileSync(outFile + '.steps.json', JSON.stringify(steps)); } catch {}
382+ await browser.close();
383+ return out;
384+}

139+pp=$(free_port); python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$www" "$pp" >"$t/plain.server.log" 2>&1 & pids+=($!)
140+wait_up() {
141+ for _ in $(seq 100); do curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$1/index.html" && return 0; sleep 0.1; done
142+ echo "FAIL: server on $1 did not start"; cat "$t"/*.server.log; exit 1
143+}
144+wait_up "$pc"; wait_up "$pp"
145+node "$here/checks/browser-boot.mjs" "http://127.0.0.1:$pc" coi "$t/native.out" >"$t/coi.json"
146+node "$here/checks/browser-boot.mjs" "http://127.0.0.1:$pp" no-coi "$t/native.out" >"$t/plain.json"
147+
148+# ---- node and wasmtime ---------------------------------------------------------
149+host_row() { # host_row <name> <hello-out> <hello-exit> <keys-out>
150+ local h=FAIL k=FAIL
151+ [ "$3" = 0 ] && cmp -s "$2" "$t/native.out" && h=PASS
152+ [ "$(cat "$4")" = "$keys_expected" ] && k=PASS
153+ printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$h" "$k"
154+}
155+LG_HOST_TIMING=1 node "$here/host/node-host.mjs" "$www/hello.wasm" </dev/null >"$t/node-hello.out" 2>"$t/node-hello.err"; nx=$?
156+node "$here/host/node-host.mjs" "$www/keys.wasm" --keys abq >"$t/node-keys.out" 2>&1
157+host_row node "$t/node-hello.out" "$nx" "$t/node-keys.out" >"$t/rows.tsv"
158+
159+feat=(--enable-gc --enable-reference-types --enable-exception-handling --enable-tail-call --enable-multivalue
160+ --enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int --enable-sign-ext --enable-mutable-globals --disable-compact-imports)
161+wasm-tools parse "$here/host/wasmtime-adapter.wat" -o "$t/adapter.wasm"
162+grep -v '(export "memory"' "$here/host/wasmtime-adapter.wat" | wasm-tools parse -o "$t/adapter-term.wasm" -
163+wt_run() { # wt_run <module> <out>; keys a b q on stdin
164+ "$MERGE" "${feat[@]}" --rename-export-conflicts "$1" main "$t/adapter.wasm" env "$t/adapter-term.wasm" term -o "$1.wt" 2>/dev/null || return 1
165+ printf 'abq' | wasmtime run -W gc=y,exceptions=y,function-references=y,tail-call=y,max-wasm-stack=268435456 \
166+ --invoke 'lw main' "$1.wt" 2>"$2.err" | grep -v '^<null anyref>$' >"$2"
167+ return "${PIPESTATUS[1]}"
168+}
169+wt_run "$www/hello.wasm" "$t/wt-hello.out"; wx=$?
170+wt_run "$www/keys.wasm" "$t/wt-keys.out"
171+host_row wasmtime "$t/wt-hello.out" "$wx" "$t/wt-keys.out" >>"$t/rows.tsv"
172+
173+# ---- report --------------------------------------------------------------------
174+python3 - "$t" <<'EOF'
175+import json, sys
176+t = sys.argv[1]
177+def ms(x): return '-' if x is None else f'{x:.1f}'
178+print(f"{'host':<16}{'COI':<6}{'SAB':<6}{'JSPI':<6}{'hello':<7}{'keys':<6}{'first-out ms':>13}{'total ms':>10}{'page-done ms':>14}")
179+def load(f):
180+ try: return json.load(open(f'{t}/{f}.json'))
181+ except Exception as e: return {'label': f, 'failure': f'no result from browser-boot.mjs ({e})'}
182+for f in ('coi', 'plain'):
183+ r = load(f)
184+ h, k = r.get('hello', {}), r.get('keys', {})
185+ print(f"{'chromium/'+r['label']:<16}{str(r.get('coi','?')):<6}{str(r.get('sab','?')):<6}{str(r.get('jspi','?')):<6}"
186+ f"{('PASS' if h.get('pass') else 'FAIL'):<7}{('PASS' if k.get('pass') else 'FAIL'):<6}"
187+ f"{ms(h.get('firstOutputMs')):>13}{ms(h.get('totalMs')):>10}{ms(h.get('pageDoneMs')):>14}")
188+ for x in ('failure',):
189+ if r.get(x): print(' ', x, r[x])
190+ for part in (h, k):
191+ if part and not part.get('pass'): print(' ', json.dumps(part)[:400])
192+timing = open(f'{t}/node-hello.err').read().strip()
193+for line in open(f'{t}/rows.tsv'):
194+ name, h, k = line.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
195+ extra = timing.replace('timing ', '') if name == 'node' else 'no JSPI: sleep/read_key block the thread'
196+ print(f"{name:<16}{'-':<6}{'-':<6}{('yes' if name=='node' else 'no'):<6}{h:<7}{k:<6} {extra}")
197+EOF
198+coi_ok=$(python3 -c '
199+import json, sys
200+try: r = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
201+except Exception: r = {}
202+print(int(bool(r.get("hello", {}).get("pass")) and bool(r.get("keys", {}).get("pass")) and r.get("coi") is True))' "$t/coi.json")
203+if [ "$coi_ok" = 1 ]; then echo "PASS (browser under COI: hello MATCHes native lg, keys echoed)"; exit 0; fi
204+echo "FAIL (browser under COI)"; exit 1

1+#!/usr/bin/env python3
2+"""census-summary.py <corpus> <raw.tsv> <bad-dir> <out.tsv> <out-summary.md> <fallbacks 0|1>
3+
4+Merges census.lg's per-unit TSV with the wasm-tools validation failures
5+(<bad-dir>/u<idx> holds the first error line), writes the final TSV and the
6+markdown summary, prints the bucket table, and exits 0 iff the P1.5 (and,
7+with fallbacks=1, P1.6) conditions hold. Stdlib only.
8+"""
9+import collections
10+import datetime
11+import os
12+import re
13+import sys
14+
15+corpus, raw, bad_dir, out_tsv, out_md, fb = sys.argv[1:7]
16+fallbacks = fb == "1"
17+
18+with open(raw) as fh:
19+ header = fh.readline().rstrip("\n").split("\t")
20+ rows = [dict(zip(header, line.rstrip("\n").split("\t"))) for line in fh if line.strip()]
21+
22+for r in rows:
23+ p = os.path.join(bad_dir, "u" + r["idx"])
24+ if os.path.exists(p):
25+ with open(p) as fh:
26+ r["detail"] = fh.read().strip()[:160]
27+ r["bucket"] = "invalid-wat"
28+
29+with open(out_tsv, "w") as fh:
30+ fh.write("\t".join(header) + "\n")
31+ for r in rows:
32+ fh.write("\t".join(r[h] for h in header) + "\n")
33+
34+COMPILES = {"ok", "unbound-var", "phase2-const"}
35+n = len(rows)
36+buckets = collections.Counter(r["bucket"] for r in rows)
37+
38+
39+def norm(b):
40+ # like failures count together: strip unit names, node ids, numbers
41+ b = re.sub(r'"u\d+_[^"]*"', '"<fn>"', b)
42+ return re.sub(r"\d+", "N", b)
43+
44+
45+heads = collections.OrderedDict()
46+for r in rows:
47+ if r["bucket"] in COMPILES:
48+ continue
49+ h = norm(r["bucket"])
50+ heads.setdefault(h, []).append(r)
51+top = sorted(heads.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1]))[:15]
52+
53+unbound = collections.Counter()
54+for r in rows:
55+ for v in filter(None, r["externs"].split(",")):
56+ unbound[v] += 1
57+p2_units = [r for r in rows if r["phase2"]]
58+p2_kinds = collections.Counter(k for r in p2_units for k in r["phase2"].split(","))
59+p2_units_by_kind = collections.Counter(k for r in p2_units for k in set(r["phase2"].split(",")))
60+
61+ops = sum(c for b, c in buckets.items() if b.startswith("unsupported op"))
62+invalid = buckets.get("invalid-wat", 0)
63+gotos = buckets.get("goto fallback", 0)
64+trees = sum(c for b, c in buckets.items() if b.startswith("unsupported tree node"))
65+compiled = sum(c for b, c in buckets.items() if b in COMPILES)
66+must = {"legmacs": [("legmacs/buffer.lg", "row-col-of")], "xsofy": [("xsofy/fov.lg", "reveal-line")]}.get(corpus, [])
67+named = []
68+for f, nm in must:
69+ hit = [r for r in rows if r["file"] == f and r["name"] == nm]
70+ named.append((f, nm, hit[0]["bucket"] if hit else "MISSING"))
71+
72+L = []
73+L.append(f"# Backend census: {corpus} ({datetime.date.today().isoformat()})\n")
74+L.append("Each top-level fn unit (one row per arity) lowered alone by lower-wasm and its "
75+ "module validated with wasm-tools; nothing is run. Regenerate with "
76+ f"`checks/census.sh {corpus}`; per-unit rows in `{corpus}.tsv`.\n")
77+L.append(f"**{compiled}/{n} units compile** ({100.0 * compiled / max(n, 1):.1f}%): "
78+ f"ok {buckets.get('ok', 0)}, unbound-var {buckets.get('unbound-var', 0)}, "
79+ f"phase2-const {buckets.get('phase2-const', 0)}. "
80+ f"unsupported op: {ops}; invalid-wat: {invalid}; goto fallback: {gotos}; unsupported tree node: {trees}.\n")
81+L.append("| bucket | units |\n|---|---:|")
82+for b, c in sorted(buckets.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])):
83+ L.append(f"| `{b}` | {c} |")
84+L.append("")
85+L.append("`unbound-var` = compiles; reaches at least one var outside the corpus with no wasm "
86+ "definition yet (a run-time `TypeError: nil is not a function `). `phase2-const` = "
87+ "compiles, no unbound var, at least one Phase-2 constant placeholder. Units reaching "
88+ "only the corpus's own vars count as ok: a whole-program compile makes those direct calls.\n")
89+L.append(f"## Top error heads ({len(heads)} distinct)\n")
90+L.append("| n | head | example | detail |\n|---:|---|---|---|")
91+for h, rs in top:
92+ ex = rs[0]
93+ d = ex["detail"].replace("|", "\\|")[:120]
94+ L.append(f"| {len(rs)} | `{h}` | {ex['file']} {ex['name']} ({ex['arity']}) | {d} |")
95+L.append("")
96+L.append(f"## Phase-2 constant placeholders: {len(p2_units)} units\n")
97+L.append("Units (any bucket) holding at least one placeholder, by kind (sites in parentheses):\n")
98+L.append("| kind | units | sites |\n|---|---:|---:|")
99+for k, c in p2_units_by_kind.most_common():
100+ L.append(f"| {k} | {c} | {p2_kinds[k]} |")
101+L.append("")
102+L.append(f"## Unbound vars: {len(unbound)} distinct (top 25 by units)\n")
103+L.append("| var | units |\n|---|---:|")
104+for v, c in unbound.most_common(25):
105+ L.append(f"| `{v}` | {c} |")
106+L.append("")
107+if named:
108+ L.append("## P1.6 named fns\n")
109+ for f, nm, b in named:
110+ L.append(f"- {f} `{nm}`: {b}")
111+ L.append("")
112+with open(out_md, "w") as fh:
113+ fh.write("\n".join(L))
114+
115+print(f"{corpus}: {compiled}/{n} compile; unsupported-op {ops}, invalid-wat {invalid}, "
116+ f"goto {gotos}, tree-node {trees}; phase2-placeholder units {len(p2_units)}")
117+for b, c in sorted(buckets.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])):
118+ print(f" {c:5d} {b}")
119+for f, nm, b in named:
120+ print(f" named: {f} {nm}: {b}")
121+
122+ok = ops == 0 and invalid == 0
123+if fallbacks:
124+ ok = ok and gotos == 0 and trees == 0 and all(b in COMPILES for _, _, b in named)
125+sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

dev/lower-wasm/checks/census.lg

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
1+;; checks/census.lg — P1.5: the 2a structurize census rerun through the backend.
2+;;
3+;; LG_SOURCE_PATHS=<corpus-root>:<lower-wasm/src> lg checks/census.lg \
4+;; <corpus-root> <corpus-name> <out.tsv> <wat-dir> <file-relative-to-root>...
5+;;
6+;; Harvesting and file loading are ../emit-wasm-probe/census/census.lg's
7+;; (analyze-ns-forms units, one per arity; nothing is evaluated but ns
8+;; requires). Each unit is expanded as the driver expands a defn, built, and
9+;; lowered ALONE by lower-wasm/lower-fn-only into a fresh session: no
10+;; signatures for the rest of the program, so every call to another var goes
11+;; through a var-table slot. The unit's complete module goes to
12+;; <wat-dir>/u<idx>.wat for census.sh to validate; nothing is run.
13+;;
14+;; Nested fn* bodies are not separate rows (census.lg's inner:* rows): the
15+;; backend lambda-lifts them while lowering the parent, so a parent's bucket
16+;; already covers every closure inside it.
17+;;
18+;; TSV columns: idx file name arity bucket detail externs program-vars phase2 ms
19+;; bucket: ok | unbound-var | phase2-const | unsupported op <op> |
20+;; unsupported tree node <tag> | goto fallback | build error <head> |
21+;; optimize error | other <first 60 chars>
22+;; ok-like buckets: unbound-var = compiles, calls/reads >=1 var outside the
23+;; corpus that has no wasm definition (Phase 2/3 native twins);
24+;; phase2-const = compiles, no unbound vars, >=1 Phase-2 constant placeholder.
25+;; externs = those out-of-corpus vars; program-vars = how many in-corpus vars
26+;; it reaches through slots (a whole-program compile makes those direct);
27+;; phase2 = the placeholder constant kinds.
28+(require 'ir.build)
29+(require 'ir.passes.pipeline)
30+(require 'lower-wasm)
31+
32+(def args (vec (rest (drop-while (fn [a] (not (clojure.string/ends-with? a "census.lg"))) os/args))))
33+(def corpus-dir (let [d (nth args 0)] (if (clojure.string/ends-with? d "/") d (str d "/"))))
34+(def corpus-name (nth args 1))
35+(def out-path (nth args 2))
36+(def wat-dir (nth args 3))
37+(def files (vec (drop 4 args)))
38+
39+;; Sharded runs (checks/census.sh, D106 item 6): LW_CENSUS_ALL names a file
40+;; listing EVERY corpus file in census order, and the positional files are this
41+;; process's share. Every process still reads, requires and declares all of
42+;; them (corpus-nses and the vars a unit can resolve are then what a serial run
43+;; sees) and numbers units over all of them, but lowers only its own. Unset,
44+;; all-files = files and nothing changes.
45+(def all-files
46+ (let [p (os/getenv "LW_CENSUS_ALL")]
47+ (if (seq p) (vec (remove empty? (clojure.string/split-lines (slurp p)))) files)))
48+(def own-files (set files))
49+
50+;; ---- file loading, as census.lg (from scripts/ir-stress.lg) -----------------
51+
52+(defn read-all [path]
53+ (try (read-code-string (str "(do " (slurp path) "\n)"))
54+ (catch e nil)))
55+
56+(defn ns-form-of [parsed]
57+ (first (filter (fn [f] (and (seq? f) (= (first f) 'ns))) (rest parsed))))
58+
59+(defn require-deps! [ns-form-]
60+ (when ns-form-
61+ (doseq [clause (drop 2 ns-form-)]
62+ (when (and (seq? clause) (= (first clause) :require))
63+ (doseq [spec (rest clause)]
64+ (try (when (or (symbol? spec) (vector? spec)) (require spec))
65+ (catch e nil)))))))
66+
67+(defn require-top-level! [parsed]
68+ (doseq [f (rest parsed)]
69+ (when (and (seq? f) (symbol? (first f))
70+ (let [h (str (first f))] (or (= h "require") (= h "use"))))
71+ (try (eval f) (catch e nil)))))
72+
73+(defn arity-units [form]
74+ (let [maybe-doc (nth form 2)
75+ has-doc? (string? maybe-doc)
76+ first-form (if has-doc? (nth form 3) maybe-doc)]
77+ (if (or (vector? first-form) (ir.build/return-hinted-arity-vector? first-form))
78+ [["1" first-form (drop (if has-doc? 4 3) form)]]
79+ (vec (map-indexed (fn [i a] [(str "m" i) (first a) (rest a)])
80+ (drop (if has-doc? 3 2) form))))))
81+
82+;; ---- classification ------------------------------------------------------------
83+
84+(defn one-line [s] (clojure.string/replace (str s) #"[\t\n\r]+" " "))
85+(defn head [s n] (let [s (one-line s)] (subs s 0 (min n (count s)))))
86+
87+(defn bucket-of
88+ "[bucket detail] for a caught exception at `stage`."
89+ [stage e]
90+ (let [m (one-line (or (ex-message e) (str e)))
91+ d (head m 160)]
92+ (cond
93+ (= stage :build) [(str "build error " (head (clojure.string/replace m #"^ir/build: " "") 40)) d]
94+ (= :optimize (:stage (ex-data e))) ["optimize error" d]
95+ :else
96+ (if-let [[_ op] (re-find #"^lower-wasm: unsupported op (:[a-z-]+)" m)]
97+ [(str "unsupported op " op) d]
98+ (if-let [[_ tag] (re-find #"^lower-wasm: unsupported tree node \{:tag (:[a-z-]+)" m)]
99+ [(str "unsupported tree node " tag) d]
100+ (if (re-find #"^lower-wasm: structurize fallback \(:goto\)" m)
101+ ["goto fallback" (head m 60)]
102+ [(str "other " (head (clojure.string/replace m #"^lower-wasm: " "") 60)) d]))))))
103+
104+(defn var-ns [v] (namespace (symbol (subs (str v) 2))))
105+
106+(def corpus-nses (atom #{}))
107+(def rows (atom []))
108+(def idx (atom 0))
109+
110+(defn run-unit [rel name arity args-vec body]
111+ (let [i (swap! idx inc)
112+ t0 (System/nanoTime)
113+ fname (str "u" i "_" name)
114+ r (try
115+ (let [src (apply list 'defn name args-vec (map lower-wasm/expand-form body))
116+ f (try (ir.build/build-fn src)
117+ (catch e (throw (ex-info "build" {::stage :build ::e e}))))
118+ ss (lower-wasm/new-session {} {})
119+ {:keys [wat externs phase2]} (lower-wasm/lower-fn-only ss fname f)
120+ outside (sort (map #(subs (str %) 2) (remove #(contains? @corpus-nses (var-ns %)) externs)))
121+ inside (count (filter #(contains? @corpus-nses (var-ns %)) externs))]
122+ (spit (str wat-dir "/u" i ".wat") (lower-wasm/session-module ss [wat]))
123+ {:bucket (cond (seq outside) "unbound-var" (seq phase2) "phase2-const" :else "ok")
124+ :externs outside :inside inside :phase2 phase2})
125+ (catch e
126+ (let [d (ex-data e)
127+ [b detail] (if (::stage d) (bucket-of :build (::e d)) (bucket-of :lower e))]
128+ {:bucket b :detail detail})))
129+ ms (quot (- (System/nanoTime) t0) 1000000)]
130+ (swap! rows conj
131+ (clojure.string/join "\t"
132+ [i rel name arity (:bucket r) (or (:detail r) "")
133+ (clojure.string/join "," (:externs r)) (or (:inside r) 0)
134+ (clojure.string/join "," (:phase2 r)) ms]))))
135+
136+(defn census-file [rel own?]
137+ (let [parsed (read-all (str corpus-dir rel))]
138+ (if (nil? parsed)
139+ (println (str "READ-ERROR " rel))
140+ (let [nsf (ns-form-of parsed)
141+ ns-sym (when nsf (nth nsf 1))]
142+ (when ns-sym (try (eval (list 'in-ns (list 'quote ns-sym))) (catch e nil)))
143+ (require-deps! nsf)
144+ (require-top-level! parsed)
145+ (let [{units :fixtures names :defined-names} (ir.passes.pipeline/analyze-ns-forms (rest parsed))]
146+ (when-let [decl (seq (remove (fn [nm] (some? (resolve nm))) names))]
147+ (try (eval (cons 'declare decl)) (catch e nil)))
148+ (doseq [u units
149+ [arity args-vec body] (arity-units u)]
150+ (if own?
151+ (run-unit rel (nth u 1) arity args-vec body)
152+ (swap! idx inc))) ; another shard lowers it; keep the serial numbering
153+ (when own? (println (str rel ": " (count units) " units"))))))))
154+
155+(defn run []
156+ (doseq [rel all-files]
157+ (try (let [parsed (read-all (str corpus-dir rel))
158+ nsf (ns-form-of parsed)]
159+ (when nsf
160+ (swap! corpus-nses conj (str (nth nsf 1)))
161+ (eval (list 'in-ns (list 'quote (nth nsf 1)))))
162+ (require-deps! nsf)
163+ (require-top-level! parsed))
164+ (catch e nil)))
165+ (doseq [rel all-files] (census-file rel (contains? own-files rel)))
166+ (spit out-path (str "idx\tfile\tname\tarity\tbucket\tdetail\texterns\tprogram-vars\tphase2\tms\n"
167+ (clojure.string/join "\n" @rows) "\n"))
168+ (println "rows:" (count @rows) "->" out-path))
169+
170+(run)
shell

@@ -0,0 +1,188 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/census.sh [--fallbacks] <corpus>... corpus = xsofy | legmacs
3+#
4+# P1.5: every top-level fn unit of the corpus (the 2a census's harvesting) is
5+# lowered ALONE by the backend (checks/census.lg, compile only, nothing runs)
6+# and its module validated with wasm-tools; a unit that lowers but does not
7+# validate is bucketed `invalid-wat`. Writes corpus/census/<corpus>.tsv and
8+# corpus/census/<corpus>-summary.md.
9+#
10+# Exit 0 iff, on every corpus, no unit is `unsupported op` or `invalid-wat`.
11+# --fallbacks (P1.6) also requires 0 `goto fallback`, 0 `unsupported tree
12+# node`, and that legmacs.buffer/row-col-of and xsofy.fov/reveal-line compile
13+# (bucket ok / unbound-var / phase2-const).
14+#
15+# Calls to vars the corpus does not define compile to calls through nil
16+# var-table slots (native's run-time `TypeError: nil is not a function `);
17+# such units count as `unbound-var`, Phase 2/3's native-twin business.
18+#
19+# D106 (6), sharded: the corpus's files are split into CENSUS_SHARDS (default
20+# 4) bins, longest-processing-time first by each file's summed `ms` in the
21+# previous TSV (file size when there is none), and one census.lg process per
22+# bin runs under checks/sem.sh. Every process still reads and declares ALL the
23+# corpus files (so the corpus-namespace set, and what each unit can resolve,
24+# are what a serial run sees) and lowers only its own share, numbering units
25+# as the serial run would (LW_CENSUS_ALL, see census.lg). The shards' rows are
26+# merged in idx order, so the TSV is the serial TSV except for the `ms`
27+# column (timings), and the summary is identical for the same day.
28+#
29+# Cache: corpus/census/<corpus>.key holds a content hash of every input
30+# (src/*.lg, rt/wasm/*.lg, checks/census.lg, checks/census-summary.py, and
31+# the name and bytes of each corpus file). When it matches, the corpus is not
32+# re-lowered: the summary and verdict are recomputed from the TSV, so
33+# checks/gate.sh's P1.5 and P1.6 rows share one census. Content, not mtime:
34+# a tree copy, a touch or a reverted edit does not invalidate it. A TSV with
35+# no .key yet is adopted once if it is newer than every input (the old rule).
36+# A per-corpus lock (corpus/census/.<corpus>.lock) makes a second census of
37+# the same corpus wait for the first and then reuse its result. FRESH=1
38+# forces a rerun.
39+#
40+# Env: LG, JOBS (parallel wasm-tools validations, default 8), CENSUS_SHARDS
41+# (default 4; 1 = one process, serial), FRESH=1, KEEP=1.
42+set -uo pipefail
43+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
44+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
45+fallbacks=0; corpora=()
46+for a in "$@"; do
47+ case $a in
48+ --fallbacks) fallbacks=1 ;;
49+ xsofy|legmacs) corpora+=("$a") ;;
50+ *) echo "usage: $0 [--fallbacks] xsofy|legmacs..." >&2; exit 2 ;;
51+ esac
52+done
53+[ ${#corpora[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--fallbacks] xsofy|legmacs..." >&2; exit 2; }
54+shards=${CENSUS_SHARDS:-4}
55+case $shards in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) echo "CENSUS_SHARDS must be a positive integer (got '$shards')" >&2; exit 2;; esac
56+t=$(mktemp -d); held=""; pids=()
57+# stop a subtree (shard subshell -> xargs -> sem.sh -> timeout -> lg) so an
58+# interrupted census leaves no workers or held slots behind
59+killtree() { local c kids; kids=$(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null); kill "$1" 2>/dev/null; for c in $kids; do killtree "$c"; done; return 0; }
60+cleanup() {
61+ local p; for p in ${pids[@]+"${pids[@]}"}; do killtree "$p"; done
62+ [ -n "$held" ] && rm -rf "$held"
63+ if [ -n "${KEEP:-}" ]; then echo "kept $t" >&2; else rm -rf "$t"; fi
64+}
65+trap cleanup EXIT
66+trap 'exit 130' INT; trap 'exit 143' TERM HUP
67+mkdir -p "$here/corpus/census"
68+
69+# mkdir lock with dead-holder reclaim (as checks/sem.sh); a second census of
70+# the same corpus blocks here until the first has written its TSV and key.
71+lock_acquire() {
72+ local d=$1 p deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + ${CENSUS_LOCK_WAIT:-3600} ))
73+ while ! mkdir "$d" 2>/dev/null; do
74+ p=$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null)
75+ if { [ -n "$p" ] && ! kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; } ||
76+ { [ -z "$p" ] && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$d" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) )) -gt 10 ]; }; then
77+ command mv "$d" "$d.dead.$$" 2>/dev/null && rm -rf "$d.dead.$$"
78+ continue
79+ fi
80+ if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then echo "census: waited for $d; running without the lock" >&2; return 0; fi
81+ sleep 1
82+ done
83+ echo $$ > "$d/pid"; held=$d
84+}
85+lock_release() { [ -n "$held" ] && rm -rf "$held"; held=""; }
86+
87+# Content hash of every input; paths are relative so a tree copy hashes the same.
88+census_key() {
89+ local root=$1 list=$2 f
90+ export LC_ALL=C
91+ {
92+ ( cd "$root" && while IFS= read -r f; do printf 'F %s\n' "$f"; cat "$f" 2>/dev/null; done < "$list" )
93+ for f in "$here"/src/*.lg "$here"/rt/wasm/*.lg "$here/checks/census.lg" "$here/checks/census-summary.py"; do
94+ printf 'F %s\n' "${f#"$here"/}"; cat "$f" 2>/dev/null
95+ done
96+ } | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1
97+}
98+
99+fail=0
100+for c in "${corpora[@]}"; do
101+ root=$HOME/projects-new/3p/$c
102+ [ -d "$root" ] || { echo "no corpus at $root" >&2; exit 2; }
103+ # same file lists as ../emit-wasm-probe/census/coverage-report.md
104+ case $c in
105+ xsofy) (cd "$root" && { echo main.lg; find xsofy -name '*.lg' | LC_ALL=C sort; }) > "$t/$c-files" ;;
106+ legmacs) (cd "$root" && { echo main.lg; find legmacs -name '*.lg' | LC_ALL=C sort; } | grep -v examples) > "$t/$c-files" ;;
107+ esac
108+ tsv=$here/corpus/census/$c.tsv
109+ keyf=$here/corpus/census/$c.key
110+ lock_acquire "$here/corpus/census/.$c.lock"
111+ key=$(census_key "$root" "$t/$c-files")
112+ reuse=0
113+ if [ -z "${FRESH:-}" ] && [ -s "$tsv" ]; then
114+ if [ -f "$keyf" ]; then
115+ [ "$(cat "$keyf")" = "$key" ] && reuse=1
116+ elif [ -z "$(cd "$root" && find $(cat "$t/$c-files") "$here"/src/*.lg "$here"/rt/wasm/*.lg \
117+ "$here/checks/census.lg" "$here/checks/census-summary.py" -newer "$tsv" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
118+ reuse=1; echo "$key" > "$keyf.tmp$$" && command mv "$keyf.tmp$$" "$keyf" # adopt a pre-key TSV once
119+ fi
120+ fi
121+ if [ $reuse -eq 1 ]; then
122+ echo "== $c: reusing $tsv (content hash of every input unchanged; FRESH=1 to rerun)"
123+ mkdir -p "$t/$c-nobad"
124+ python3 "$here/checks/census-summary.py" "$c" "$tsv" "$t/$c-nobad" "$t/$c.tsv" \
125+ "$here/corpus/census/$c-summary.md" "$fallbacks" || fail=1
126+ lock_release
127+ continue
128+ fi
129+ mkdir -p "$t/$c-wat"
130+ nfiles=$(wc -l < "$t/$c-files" | tr -d ' ')
131+ echo "== $c: $nfiles files"
132+ # LPT bins by the previous TSV's per-file ms (size when absent or incomplete)
133+ python3 - "$t/$c-files" "$tsv" "$shards" "$t/$c-shard" "$root" >/dev/null <<'PYEOF'
134+import os, sys
135+listf, prev, n, prefix, root = sys.argv[1:6]
136+files = [l.rstrip("\n") for l in open(listf) if l.strip()]
137+w = {}
138+try:
139+ with open(prev) as fh:
140+ hdr = fh.readline().rstrip("\n").split("\t")
141+ fi, mi = hdr.index("file"), hdr.index("ms")
142+ for line in fh:
143+ p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
144+ if len(p) > mi and p[mi].isdigit():
145+ w[p[fi]] = w.get(p[fi], 0) + int(p[mi])
146+except (OSError, ValueError):
147+ w = {}
148+if any(f not in w for f in files): # a new or unmeasured file: sizes for all
149+ w = {f: os.path.getsize(os.path.join(root, f)) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) else 0 for f in files}
150+n = max(1, min(int(n), len(files)))
151+bins = [[0, []] for _ in range(n)]
152+for f in sorted(files, key=lambda f: (-w[f], f)):
153+ b = min(bins, key=lambda b: b[0])
154+ b[0] += w[f]; b[1].append(f)
155+for k, (_, fs) in enumerate(bins):
156+ with open(f"{prefix}.{k}", "w") as out:
157+ out.write("\n".join(f for f in files if f in set(fs)) + "\n")
158+print(n)
159+PYEOF
160+ nshards=$(ls "$t/$c-shard".* 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
161+ # the corpus must be the cwd: its main.lg loads siblings relative to it
162+ pids=()
163+ for ((k=0; k<nshards; k++)); do
164+ ( cd "$root" && LG_SOURCE_PATHS="$root:$here/src" LW_CENSUS_ALL="$t/$c-files" \
165+ xargs "$here/checks/sem.sh" timeout 3600 "$LG" "$here/checks/census.lg" \
166+ "$root" "$c" "$t/$c.raw.$k.tsv" "$t/$c-wat" < "$t/$c-shard.$k" ) > "$t/$c.log.$k" 2>&1 &
167+ pids+=($!)
168+ done
169+ for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p"; done
170+ for ((k=0; k<nshards; k++)); do
171+ [ -s "$t/$c.raw.$k.tsv" ] || { echo "census.lg failed for $c (shard $k):"; tail -20 "$t/$c.log.$k"; exit 1; }
172+ done
173+ # merge the shards' rows in idx order (header from shard 0)
174+ { head -1 "$t/$c.raw.0.tsv"
175+ for ((k=0; k<nshards; k++)); do tail -n +2 "$t/$c.raw.$k.tsv"; done | grep -v '^$' | sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k1,1n -s
176+ } > "$t/$c.raw.tsv"
177+ # validate every unit module that lowered; first error line per failure
178+ mkdir -p "$t/$c-bad"
179+ find "$t/$c-wat" -name '*.wat' -print0 | xargs -0 -P "${JOBS:-8}" -n 1 sh -c \
180+ 'wasm-tools validate "$1" >/dev/null 2>"$1.err" || { b=$(basename "$1" .wat); head -1 "$1.err" > "'"$t/$c-bad"'/$b"; }; rm -f "$1.err"' _
181+ python3 "$here/checks/census-summary.py" "$c" "$t/$c.raw.tsv" "$t/$c-bad" \
182+ "$tsv" "$here/corpus/census/$c-summary.md" "$fallbacks"
183+ prc=$?
184+ [ $prc -le 1 ] && [ -s "$tsv" ] && { echo "$key" > "$keyf.tmp$$" && command mv "$keyf.tmp$$" "$keyf"; }
185+ [ $prc -eq 0 ] || fail=1
186+ lock_release
187+done
188+exit $fail
shell

+71 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/gate.sh <phase> — every item of the phase must exit 0 (not 2).
3+#
4+# D106 (1c): the phase's rows run LW_GATE_J at a time (default 2; 1 = one
5+# after another). Same rows, same exit rule, same "ok <id>" / "FAIL <id>
6+# (exit n)" lines in items.tsv order (printed as soon as a row and every row
7+# before it have finished). The difference from the old serial gate: each
8+# row's output is KEPT in ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-gate-<phase>/<id>.log instead of
9+# discarded, so a FAIL says where to look (on stderr, so stdout is unchanged)
10+# rather than meaning "rerun the row to see why". Two gates of the same phase
11+# running at once share that directory and overwrite each other's logs.
12+# Rows are not wrapped in the slot pool (checks/sem.sh) themselves: a gate
13+# holding a slot per row while the rows' own workers wait for slots could
14+# deadlock several agents' gates against each other. The heavy leaves
15+# (oracle programs, census shards, native test files) take slots instead.
16+set -uo pipefail
17+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
18+ph=${1:?phase}; fail=0
19+# D51: the gate runs the slow tier too. SLOW=1 makes the native runtime check
20+# (P2.9's row) run its default assertions plus the 10k map/set builds, every
21+# path at 1000 keys and the 1e6 reduce gate, so one pass covers both tiers.
22+[ "$ph" = 2 ] && export SLOW=1
23+j=${LW_GATE_J:-2}
24+case $j in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) echo "LW_GATE_J must be a positive integer (got '$j')" >&2; exit 2;; esac
25+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
26+ids=()
27+while IFS= read -r id; do ids+=("$id"); done < <(awk -F'\t' -v p="$ph" '$1 !~ /^#/ && $2==p && $1 !~ /GATE/{print $1}' checks/items.tsv)
28+[ ${#ids[@]} -gt 0 ] || exit 0
29+
30+logd=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}; logd=${logd%/}/lw-gate-$ph; mkdir -p "$logd"
31+rcd=$(mktemp -d); xp=""
32+# stop a whole subtree (xargs -> sem.sh -> worker -> lg), parent first so xargs
33+# starts no replacement, so an interrupted run
34+# leaves no workers or held slots behind
35+killtree() { local c kids; kids=$(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null); kill "$1" 2>/dev/null; for c in $kids; do killtree "$c"; done; return 0; }
36+trap 'for c in $(pgrep -P $$ 2>/dev/null); do killtree "$c"; done; rm -rf "$rcd"' EXIT
37+trap 'exit 130' INT; trap 'exit 143' TERM HUP
38+export logd rcd
39+for id in "${ids[@]}"; do rm -f "$logd/$id.log"; done
40+
41+# Build the rtlib once before rows fan out: two rows starting cold would each
42+# build it (45-175 s, CPU only, identical output). Same newer-than guess as
43+# checks/run-corpus.sh: a wrong guess costs one compile, never a wrong result.
44+if [ "$j" -gt 1 ] && [ -x checks/wasm-run.sh ]; then
45+ d=${LW_RTLIB_DIR:-src/.rtlib}
46+ newest=$(ls -t "$d"/rtlib-*.edn 2>/dev/null | head -1)
47+ if [ -z "$newest" ] || [ -n "$(find src rt/wasm -name '*.lg' -newer "$newest" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then
48+ w=$(mktemp -d)
49+ checks/sem.sh "$LG" -source-paths src src/driver.lg corpus/scalar/fib.clj "$w/m.wat" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
50+ wait $! # (background + wait: a TERM during the build reaches the trap at once)
51+ rm -rf "$w"
52+ fi
53+fi
54+
55+row() {
56+ checks/run.sh "$1" >"$logd/$1.log" 2>&1
57+ echo $? >"$rcd/$1.tmp"; command mv "$rcd/$1.tmp" "$rcd/$1.rc"
58+}
59+export -f row
60+printf '%s\0' "${ids[@]}" | xargs -0 -n 1 -P "$j" bash -c 'row "$1"' _ &
61+xp=$!
62+for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
63+ while [ ! -e "$rcd/$id.rc" ]; do
64+ kill -0 "$xp" 2>/dev/null || break
65+ sleep 0.3
66+ done
67+ rc=$(cat "$rcd/$id.rc" 2>/dev/null || echo 99)
68+ if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then echo "ok $id"; else echo "FAIL $id (exit $rc)"; echo "gate: $id output kept in $logd/$id.log" >&2; fail=1; fi
69+done
70+wait "$xp" 2>/dev/null; xp=""
71+exit $fail
shell
