@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/hash-parity.sh [--self] [vectors.tsv] — item P2.2.
3+#
4+# Default: for each row of corpus/hash/vectors.tsv (kind, edn, hash from
5+# let-go's vm.HashValue), ask the wasm runtime for the hash via
6+# checks/wasm-hash.sh <edn> <kind>
7+# which must print the decimal uint32 hash of (read-string edn) and nothing
8+# else. kind is passed because one EDN text can name two runtime types:
9+# "pvector" rows are PersistentVectors (what a vector with metadata becomes),
10+# and [] hashes differently as a PersistentVector than as an ArrayVector.
11+#
12+# --self: recompute every row through native lg's `hash` builtin, in ONE lg
13+# process, and compare with the Go table. This proves the table is what lg
14+# itself computes, and is the falsification path for the table's format.
15+#
16+# Exit: 0 = every row matches; 1 = at least one miss; 2 = hook missing.
17+set -uo pipefail
18+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
19+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
20+
21+self=0
22+if [ "${1:-}" = --self ]; then self=1; shift; fi
23+tsv=${1:-$here/../corpus/hash/vectors.tsv}
24+[ -r "$tsv" ] || { echo "no vectors file: $tsv"; exit 2; }
25+tsv=$(cd "$(dirname "$tsv")" && pwd)/$(basename "$tsv")
26+
27+if [ "$self" = 1 ]; then
28+ # lg prints one MISS line per mismatch and a final "ROWS <n> MISSES <m>".
29+ out=$("$LG" -e "
30+(require '[clojure.string :as str])
31+(let [rows (->> (str/split-lines (slurp \"$tsv\"))
32+ (remove #(or (str/blank? %) (str/starts-with? % \"#\")))
33+ (map #(str/split % #\"\t\")))
34+ misses (atom 0)]
35+ (doseq [[kind edn want] rows]
36+ (let [v (read-string edn)
37+ v (if (= kind \"pvector\") (with-meta v {:pv true}) v)
38+ got (hash v)]
39+ (when (not= got (parse-long want))
40+ (swap! misses inc)
41+ (println \"MISS\" kind edn \"want\" want \"got\" got))))
42+ (println \"ROWS\" (count rows) \"MISSES\" @misses))
43+" 2>&1)
44+ printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^nil$'
45+ summary=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep '^ROWS ')
46+ [ -n "$summary" ] || { echo "FAIL: lg did not finish"; exit 1; }
47+ set -- $summary
48+ [ "$4" = 0 ] && { echo "OK: lg hash == vm.HashValue on all $2 rows"; exit 0; }
49+ echo "FAIL: $4 of $2 rows differ"; exit 1
50+fi
51+
52+hook=${WASM_HASH:-$here/wasm-hash.sh} # override to test the loop
53+[ -x "$hook" ] || { echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED: $hook missing"; exit 2; }
54+rows=0 misses=0 limits=0
55+while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind edn want; do
56+ case $kind in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
57+ rows=$((rows + 1))
58+ got=$("$hook" "$edn" "$kind" 2>&1)
59+ # LIMIT = the runtime names this kind a Phase-2 limit (bigint/ratio/bigdec, D15): skipped, reported, not a miss.
60+ if [ "$got" = LIMIT ]; then limits=$((limits + 1)); echo "LIMIT $kind ${edn:0:60}"; continue; fi
61+ if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
62+ misses=$((misses + 1))
63+ echo "MISS $kind ${edn:0:80} want $want got ${got:0:80}"
64+ fi
65+done < "$tsv"
66+echo "ROWS $rows MISSES $misses LIMITS $limits"
67+[ "$misses" = 0 ]

dev/lower-wasm/checks/intrinsics-native-runner.lg

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
1+;; Runs P2.1's native half: corpus/intrinsics/*_test.lg against the reference
2+;; intrinsics. Invoked by checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh with the expected
3+;; deftest count, so a file that silently registers no tests fails the check.
4+;; Uses run-all-tests with a regex, never bare (run-tests): on let-go 1.13 that
5+;; tests only the CURRENT ns (here `user`) and reports 0 tests, exit 0.
6+;; The test namespaces arrive after the count, one per *_test.lg file, so a
7+;; new file needs no edit here.
8+(def ^:private test-nss (mapv symbol (rest *command-line-args*)))
9+(apply require test-nss)
10+
11+(let [expected (parse-long (first *command-line-args*))
12+ s (test/run-all-tests (re-pattern (str "(" (apply str (interpose "|" test-nss)) ")")))
13+ ok (and (test/successful? s) (pos? (:test s)) (= expected (:test s)))]
14+ (println (str "intrinsics-native: tests=" (:test s) " (expected " expected ")"
15+ " pass=" (:pass s) " fail=" (:fail s) " error=" (:error s)
16+ (if ok " OK" " FAILED")))
17+ (os/exit (if ok 0 1)))

3+# the stock-Go lane after the same scripted play, at seed 424242.
4+#
5+# Lanes:
6+# stock xsofy main.lg bundled by `lg -w -w-shell none` at let-go 4e769212
7+# (the backend's ground truth, LETGO_SRC = a `git archive` export of
8+# that commit, so the canonical let-go checkout is not touched), then
9+# xsofy-shell.html injected by local-scripts/inject-shell.sh: exactly
10+# local-scripts/build-bundle.sh's client-shell path. Cached under
11+# $LW_LANE5_CACHE keyed by the commit, xsofy's sources and the shell.
12+# lw host/build-xsofy-module.sh's module.wasm in host/build-xsofy-serve.sh's
13+# page (the same shell, injected the same way, on the adapter).
14+# Both are served with COOP/COEP (local-scripts/coi-serve.py): the stock lane's
15+# key ring needs SharedArrayBuffer; the lw lane does not care (D91).
16+#
17+# Walks, each run on both lanes and compared with cmp (document.body.innerText):
18+# probe GATE. browser-boot.mjs --settle-walk: zz-determinism-probe.mjs's key
19+# sequence (?seed=, title, Space, map, 3 s, then l l j j h k l j), but a
20+# key is sent only after the game finished the previous one (its
21+# xsofy/stats event arrived, then the xterm rows held still for 3 x
22+# 100 ms). The probe's own 400 ms spacing made the result depend on
23+# machine load (run A probe IDENTICAL/held DIFFER, run B the reverse at
24+# load 15-45): both lanes coalesce identical queued keys, so whether a
25+# key lands mid-turn changes the dump in BOTH lanes. A wait that times
26+# out is a HARNESS failure (reported as such), not a lane mismatch.
27+# held INFORMATIONAL, never affects the exit code. checks/browser-boot.mjs
28+# --walk: the same boot, then auto-repeat bursts (n keydowns in one
29+# task) that let-go's ring coalesces into one read (D98). Coalescing is
30+# timing-dependent by design in both lanes, so the screens cannot be a
31+# byte-identity gate; the deterministic half (a 5-key burst is ONE read)
32+# is gated by checks/browser-boot.sh --xsofy-shell's `held` assertion.
33+# No masking: neither lane has build-info.json, so the shell prints the same
34+# chrome; the title bar and quest come from xsofy/startup on both.
35+# Exit 0 iff the probe walk is byte-identical across the lanes; 2 on a harness
36+# failure (walk timeout / crash), 1 on a lane mismatch.

45+COMMIT=4e769212
46+SEED=${SEED:-424242}
47+pw=$ws/local-scripts/browser-smoke-playwright

51+
52+# ---- stock lane ------------------------------------------------------------------

55+ find "$XSOFY/xsofy" -name '*.lg' -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 cat; } | md5 -q)

72+

76+pl=$(free_port); python3 "$ws/local-scripts/coi-serve.py" "$pl" "$t/lw" >"$t/l.log" 2>&1 & pids+=($!)

86+ || echo "note: held walk on $lane crashed (informational)"

91+ echo "$w IDENTICAL $(wc -c <"$t/$w-lw.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes, md5 $(md5 -q "$t/$w-lw.txt")"

94+ grep -h failure "$t/$w-stock.json" "$t/$w-lw.json" 2>/dev/null
95+ [ "$w" = probe ] && ok=0

97+done

99+# per-key turn counter (a key that coalesced shows turn +0)
100+python3 - "$t/probe-stock.txt.steps.json" "$t/probe-lw.txt.steps.json" <<'PY'
101+import json, sys
102+try: a, b = (json.load(open(f)) for f in sys.argv[1:3])
103+except Exception: sys.exit(0)

105+ print(" probe %-5s turns %s ack ms %s" % (name, " ".join("%s:%s>%s" % (s["key"], s["turnBefore"], s["turnAfter"]) for s in st), [s["ackMs"] for s in st]))
106+for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(a, b)):
107+ if x["rows"] != y["rows"]:

110+echo "walks: probe (gate) = l l j j h k l j, each after the game settled; held (informational) = $(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("bursts","?"))' "$t/held-lw.json" 2>/dev/null) (one task per burst)"
111+if [ "$harness" = 1 ]; then echo "FAIL (lane 5: harness failure, not a lane mismatch)"; exit 2; fi
112+if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then echo "PASS (lane 5 probe walk byte-identical to the stock-Go lane at seed $SEED)"; exit 0; fi

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/map-order.sh [--native | --update] — the P2.4 check.
3+#
4+# Default (the items.tsv row): both halves must pass.
5+# 1. checks/run-corpus.sh corpus/maporder — every map/set iteration-order
6+# program MATCHes native lg under the backend (STALE-EXPECTED first).
7+# 2. let-go's test/map_order_test.lg under the backend via
8+# checks/run-tests.sh. That runner does not exist yet: the half prints
9+# NOT IMPLEMENTED and the check exits 2.
10+# Exit: 0 both pass; 1 any MISMATCH / STALE-EXPECTED / test failure;
11+# 2 otherwise not done (backend or runner missing).
12+#
13+# --native check the corpus itself, no backend: regenerate the programs into
14+# a scratch dir with gen.lg and require them byte-identical to the
15+# committed ones, then require native lg's stdout to equal every
16+# .expected. Exit 0 clean, 1 on any drift. Writes nothing.
17+# --update regenerate the programs in place and rewrite every .expected.
18+#
19+# Env: LG (native lg; default = the plan's pinned main build),
20+# LETGO (let-go checkout holding test/map_order_test.lg).
21+set -uo pipefail
22+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
23+cd "$root"
24+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
25+LETGO=${LETGO:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/let-go}
26+export LG
27+dir=corpus/maporder
28+
29+programs() { find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.lg' ! -name gen.lg | LC_ALL=C sort; }
30+
31+case "${1:-}" in
32+ --update)
33+ "$LG" "$dir/gen.lg" "$dir/" || exit 1
34+ while IFS= read -r f; do
35+ "$LG" "$f" >"$f.expected" || { echo "native lg exited $? on $f" >&2; exit 1; }
36+ done < <(programs)
37+ echo "wrote $(programs | wc -l | tr -d ' ') .expected files"
38+ exit 0 ;;
39+ --native)
40+ t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
41+ bad=0
42+ "$LG" "$dir/gen.lg" "$t/" >/dev/null || { echo "FAIL gen.lg"; exit 1; }
43+ # generator drift: the committed programs must be exactly what gen.lg writes
44+ for g in "$t"/*.lg; do
45+ b=$(basename "$g")
46+ if ! cmp -s "$g" "$dir/$b"; then echo "STALE-PROGRAM $dir/$b"; bad=1; fi
47+ done
48+ n=0
49+ while IFS= read -r f; do
50+ n=$((n+1))
51+ [ -e "$t/$(basename "$f")" ] || { echo "ORPHAN-PROGRAM $f (gen.lg no longer writes it)"; bad=1; }
52+ if [ ! -e "$f.expected" ]; then echo "MISSING-EXPECTED $f"; bad=1; continue; fi
53+ "$LG" "$f" >"$t/out" 2>/dev/null
54+ if cmp -s "$f.expected" "$t/out"; then
55+ echo "OK $f ($(wc -l <"$f.expected" | tr -d ' ') lines)"
56+ else
57+ echo "STALE-EXPECTED $f"; diff "$f.expected" "$t/out" | head -4 | sed 's/^/ /'; bad=1
58+ fi
59+ done < <(programs)
60+ echo "$n programs checked natively"
61+ exit $bad ;;
62+ "") ;;
63+ *) echo "usage: $0 [--native | --update]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
64+esac
65+
66+checks/run-corpus.sh "$dir"; corpus_rc=$?
67+
68+test_file=$LETGO/test/map_order_test.lg
69+if [ -x checks/run-tests.sh ]; then
70+ checks/run-tests.sh "$test_file"; tests_rc=$?
71+else
72+ echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED $test_file (checks/run-tests.sh missing)"; tests_rc=2
73+fi
74+
75+[ $corpus_rc -eq 1 ] || [ $tests_rc -eq 1 ] && exit 1
76+[ $corpus_rc -eq 0 ] && [ $tests_rc -eq 0 ] && exit 0
77+exit 2

1+;; checks/run-tests.sh's native side: load one test file by path and run its
2+;; namespace's tests with test/run-tests, after taking the :test off every
3+;; deftest named in the skip list (the same ones the backend side leaves out),
4+;; so the summary lines compare like for like.
5+;; lg -source-paths <paths> checks/native-test-runner.lg <file.lg> [skip ...]
6+;; Loading by path, not `require`, is what let-go's own harness does
7+;; (test/language_test.go executes each file): a file whose ns does not
8+;; match its name (chunked_seq_test.lg declares test.chunked-seq) runs too.
9+;; An ns symbol instead of a path is still accepted (required as before).
10+(let [[target & skips] *command-line-args*
11+ skips (map symbol skips)
12+ ns-name (if (clojure.string/ends-with? target ".lg")
13+ (let [forms (read-string (str "[" (slurp target) "\n]"))
14+ n (some #(when (and (seq? %) (= 'ns (first %))) (second %)) forms)]
15+ (binding [*file* target] (load-string (slurp target)))
16+ n)
17+ (let [n (symbol target)] (require n) n))]
18+ (doseq [s skips]
19+ (when-let [v (get (ns-interns ns-name) s)] (alter-meta! v dissoc :test)))
20+ (test/run-tests ns-name))

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/native-twins.sh <reach-list> [--manifest FILE] [--exclude REGEX] — the P2.8/P3.1 check.
3+#
4+# For a reach list (one `ns/name` per line, as tools/reach.sh writes), print
5+# every native with no wasm twin, grouped by ns, with the inventory's arity,
6+# source and registration columns, then `MISSING n / REACHED m`.
7+# Exit 0 iff n = 0; 1 otherwise; 2 when an input is missing.
8+#
9+# Twins come from the real manifest (`tools/twin-manifest.lg`: `:twin`
10+# metadata on rt/wasm defns). Until any marker exists it falls back to
11+# corpus/natives/manifest-proposed.tsv under a PROPOSED MANIFEST banner.
12+# --manifest FILE overrides both (TSV, twin in column 1; used to falsify).
13+# --exclude REGEX drops reach-list entries matching the (awk ERE) regex
14+# before scoring, e.g. --exclude 'term/' (D58: term/* is Phase 4); they are
15+# counted on an EXCLUDED line, never as reached.
16+#
17+# A twin covers every var bound to the same NativeFn (the inventory's
18+# same-fn-as column): a twin for core/trim covers string/trim.
19+#
20+# A bare file name that does not exist is looked up in corpus/natives/, so
21+# `corpus/natives-shared.txt` (the items.tsv spelling) resolves too.
22+#
23+# Env: LG (native lg; default = the plan's pinned main build),
24+# RT (runtime sources scanned for markers; default rt/wasm).
25+set -uo pipefail
26+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
27+cd "$root"
28+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
29+inv=corpus/natives/inventory.tsv
30+
31+reach=${1:?usage: checks/native-twins.sh <reach-list> [--manifest FILE] [--exclude REGEX]}
32+shift
33+manifest_override=
34+exclude=
35+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
36+ case $1 in
37+ --manifest) manifest_override=${2:?--manifest needs a file}; shift 2 ;;
38+ --exclude) exclude=${2:?--exclude needs a regex}; shift 2 ;;
39+ *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
40+ esac
41+done
42+
43+if [ ! -f "$reach" ] && [ -f "corpus/natives/${reach##*/}" ]; then
44+ reach=corpus/natives/${reach##*/}
45+fi
46+[ -f "$reach" ] || { echo "no reach list: $reach" >&2; exit 2; }
47+[ -f "$inv" ] || { echo "no inventory: $inv (run tools/native-inventory.lg)" >&2; exit 2; }
48+
49+tmp=$(mktemp -d)
50+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
51+
52+if [ -n "$manifest_override" ]; then
53+ [ -f "$manifest_override" ] || { echo "no manifest: $manifest_override" >&2; exit 2; }
54+ grep -v '^#' "$manifest_override" > "$tmp/manifest"
55+ echo "manifest: $manifest_override (override)"
56+else
57+ "$LG" tools/twin-manifest.lg "${RT:-rt/wasm}" > "$tmp/manifest" || { echo "tools/twin-manifest.lg failed" >&2; exit 2; }
58+ if [ -s "$tmp/manifest" ]; then
59+ echo "manifest: :twin markers in ${RT:-rt/wasm} ($(wc -l < "$tmp/manifest" | tr -d ' ') claims)"
60+ else
61+ grep -v '^#' corpus/natives/manifest-proposed.tsv > "$tmp/manifest"
62+ echo "################################################################"
63+ echo "# PROPOSED MANIFEST: no :twin markers in rt/wasm yet; using"
64+ echo "# corpus/natives/manifest-proposed.tsv (name-matched, every"
65+ echo "# confidence counted, low included). Not a claim by the runtime."
66+ echo "################################################################"
67+ fi
68+fi
69+echo "inventory: $(head -1 "$inv" | sed 's/^# native inventory: //')"
70+echo "reach list: $reach"
71+[ -n "$exclude" ] && echo "exclude: $exclude"
72+
73+awk -F'\t' -v invf="$inv" -v manf="$tmp/manifest" -v ex="$exclude" '
74+ BEGIN {
75+ while ((getline l < invf) > 0) {
76+ if (l ~ /^#/) continue
77+ split(l, c, "\t")
78+ ar[c[1]] = c[2]; src[c[1]] = c[3]; via[c[1]] = c[4]
79+ grp[c[1]] = (c[6] != "" && c[6] != "-") ? c[6] : c[1]
80+ }
81+ while ((getline l < manf) > 0) {
82+ split(l, c, "\t")
83+ if (c[1] == "") continue
84+ g = (c[1] in grp) ? grp[c[1]] : c[1]
85+ claimed[g] = 1
86+ if (!(c[1] in grp)) bogus[c[1]] = 1
87+ }
88+ for (b in bogus) printf "WARN manifest claims %s, which is not a native in the inventory\n", b
89+ }
90+ /^[ \t]*$/ { next }
91+ ex != "" && $1 ~ ex { excluded++; next }
92+ {
93+ q = $1; reached++
94+ g = (q in grp) ? grp[q] : q
95+ if (g in claimed) next
96+ i = index(q, "/"); ns = (i > 1) ? substr(q, 1, i - 1) : "?"
97+ if (!(q in grp)) ns = "NOT IN INVENTORY"
98+ line = sprintf(" %-36s %-8s %-40s %s", q, (q in ar) ? ar[q] : "?", (q in src) ? src[q] : "?", (q in via) ? via[q] : "?")
99+ rows[ns] = rows[ns] line "\n"; cnt[ns]++; missing++
100+ }
101+ END {
102+ n = 0
103+ for (ns in cnt) keys[++n] = ns
104+ # largest group first, then by name
105+ for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) for (j = i + 1; j <= n; j++)
106+ if (cnt[keys[j]] > cnt[keys[i]] || (cnt[keys[j]] == cnt[keys[i]] && keys[j] < keys[i])) { t = keys[i]; keys[i] = keys[j]; keys[j] = t }
107+ for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) { printf "== %s (%d)\n%s", keys[i], cnt[keys[i]], rows[keys[i]] }
108+ if (excluded > 0) printf "EXCLUDED %d (%s)\n", excluded, ex
109+ printf "MISSING %d / REACHED %d\n", missing + 0, reached + 0
110+ exit (missing > 0) ? 1 : 0
111+ }
112+' "$reach"
shell

dev/lower-wasm/checks/oracle.sh

+38 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# The match relation for every differential check in this plan.
3+#
4+# checks/oracle.sh <program.lg> [args...]
5+#
6+# Runs the program under native lg and under the wasm backend, and declares
7+# a MATCH only when all three agree:
8+# 1. stdout, byte for byte;
9+# 2. exit class: both 0, or both non-zero;
10+# 3. on non-zero exit, the first line of stderr after normalisation
11+# (paths, addresses and "at <file>:<line>" suffixes stripped), so a
12+# program that throws must throw the same error, not merely fail.
13+# Prints MATCH or MISMATCH <which> and exits 0/1. Nothing else counts as
14+# "matches" anywhere in the plan.
15+#
16+# Env: LG (native lg; default = the plan's pinned main build), LG_ARGS (args before the program),
17+# WASM_RUN (command that compiles+runs an .lg through the backend and
18+# behaves like lg on stdout/stderr/exit; unset = NOT IMPLEMENTED, exit 2),
19+# KEEP=1 to leave the scratch dir behind.
20+set -uo pipefail
21+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
22+prog=$1; shift
23+[ -n "${WASM_RUN:-}" ] || { echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED: WASM_RUN unset (backend runner missing)"; exit 2; }
24+t=$(mktemp -d); trap '[ -n "${KEEP:-}" ] || rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
25+norm() { sed -E -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' -e 's#(/[^ :]+)+/##g' -e 's/0x[0-9a-f]+/0xADDR/g' -e 's/ at [^ ]+:[0-9]+//g' -e 's/:[0-9]+:[0-9]+$//' | grep -m1 -i 'error' ; }
26+# LG_ARGS: extra native-lg args before the program (e.g. -source-paths <root>); split on whitespace by design.
27+"$LG" ${LG_ARGS:-} "$prog" "$@" >"$t/n.out" 2>"$t/n.err"; nx=$?
28+$WASM_RUN "$prog" "$@" >"$t/w.out" 2>"$t/w.err"; wx=$?
29+if [ "$((nx==0))" != "$((wx==0))" ]; then echo "MISMATCH exit ($nx vs $wx)"; exit 1; fi
30+if [ $nx -eq 0 ]; then
31+ if ! cmp -s "$t/n.out" "$t/w.out"; then echo "MISMATCH stdout"; diff "$t/n.out" "$t/w.out" | head -5; exit 1; fi
32+else
33+ # lg prints its error report to STDOUT with ANSI colour, file:line:col and a
34+ # source excerpt; compare the normalised first error line of all output.
35+ ne=$(cat "$t/n.out" "$t/n.err" | norm); we=$(cat "$t/w.out" "$t/w.err" | norm)
36+ if [ "$ne" != "$we" ]; then echo "MISMATCH error"; echo " native: $ne"; echo " wasm: $we"; exit 1; fi
37+fi
38+echo MATCH
shell

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/refuse.sh <dir> — P1.4. Every program in <dir> carries a header line
3+# ;; refuse: <text>
4+# naming the error the backend must refuse it with. For each program:
5+# 1. the driver alone (the compile step of wasm-run.sh) must fail, so the
6+# refusal is at compile time, not a run-time throw;
7+# 2. checks/wasm-run.sh must exit non-zero;
8+# 3. the first `error:` line of its output must read `lower-wasm: <text>`.
9+# Prints one line per program (REFUSED / ACCEPTED / WRONG-ERROR / NO-HEADER)
10+# and exits 0 iff every program was refused as documented.
11+#
12+# corpus/refused holds three (as of 2026-10-01): dot-interop (:dot), infn-def
13+# (:def in a fn), set-var (:set-var). P1.4's fourth, the variadic `& args`
14+# defn, compiles since P2.12 (D83) and moved to corpus/closure/variadic.lg.
15+#
16+# A program may instead carry
17+# ;; refuse-runtime: <text>
18+# (P1.7) when the refusal can only happen at run time (whether a printed
19+# value is a fn is not known statically): the driver must then COMPILE it,
20+# and steps 2 and 3 apply unchanged. A program carrying both headers is
21+# NO-HEADER (ambiguous).
22+set -uo pipefail
23+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
24+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
25+dir=${1:?usage: refuse.sh <dir>}
26+t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
27+n=0; ok=0
28+for f in $(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.lg' -o -name '*.clj' \) | LC_ALL=C sort); do
29+ n=$((n+1))
30+ want=$(sed -n 's/^;; refuse: //p' "$f" | head -1)
31+ wantrt=$(sed -n 's/^;; refuse-runtime: //p' "$f" | head -1)
32+ if [ -n "$want" ] && [ -n "$wantrt" ]; then echo "NO-HEADER $f (both refuse: and refuse-runtime:)"; continue; fi
33+ if [ -z "$want" ] && [ -z "$wantrt" ]; then echo "NO-HEADER $f"; continue; fi
34+ if [ -n "$want" ]; then
35+ if "$LG" -source-paths "$here/src" "$here/src/driver.lg" "$f" "$t/m.wat" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36+ echo "ACCEPTED $f (the driver compiled it; want: $want)"; continue
37+ fi
38+ else
39+ want=$wantrt
40+ if ! "$LG" -source-paths "$here/src" "$here/src/driver.lg" "$f" "$t/m.wat" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41+ echo "COMPILE-FAIL $f (want a run-time refusal: $want)"; continue
42+ fi
43+ fi
44+ "$here/checks/wasm-run.sh" "$f" >"$t/out" 2>&1; x=$?
45+ if [ $x -eq 0 ]; then echo "ACCEPTED $f (wasm-run exited 0)"; continue; fi
46+ first=$(sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$t/out" | grep -m1 '^error:' | sed 's/^error: //')
47+ case "$first" in
48+ "lower-wasm: $want"*) echo "REFUSED $f: $first"; ok=$((ok+1)) ;;
49+ *) echo "WRONG-ERROR $f: want 'lower-wasm: $want', got '$first'" ;;
50+ esac
51+done
52+echo "$ok/$n refused as documented"
53+[ $n -gt 0 ] && [ $ok -eq $n ]
shell

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/run-corpus.sh [--both] [--update-expected] <dir>...
3+#
4+# For every *.lg / *.clj in the given dirs, run
5+# WASM_RUN=checks/wasm-run.sh checks/oracle.sh <file>
6+# and print one line per file: MATCH, MISMATCH, NOT IMPLEMENTED, or
7+# STALE-EXPECTED. Then "n/total MATCH".
8+#
9+# oracle.sh is the match relation (it reruns native lg itself). A <file>.expected
10+# next to a program is a committed snapshot of native lg's stdout: it is checked
11+# first, and a difference is STALE-EXPECTED (counts as a failure), so a hand-edit
12+# or an lg that changed behaviour under the corpus is caught even before any
13+# backend exists. Files without .expected skip that step.
14+#
15+# Exit: 0 all MATCH; 1 any MISMATCH or STALE-EXPECTED; 2 otherwise not all
16+# MATCH because the backend (checks/wasm-run.sh) is missing or unimplemented.
17+#
18+# --update-expected rewrite every .expected from native lg and exit
19+# (programs that already have one, plus all of opmatrix/).
20+# --both P2.1: a *_test.lg file (deftests) MATCHes only when it
21+# passes (a) under native lg with the reference intrinsics
22+# (checks/intrinsics-native-runner.lg, deftest-count
23+# guard) AND (b) through the backend (checks/run-tests.sh:
24+# same summary and FAIL/ERROR lines as native run-tests).
25+# Other programs still go through oracle.sh.
26+#
27+# Env: LG (native lg; default = the plan's pinned main build).
28+# LW_PAR programs run at once (default 3; LW_PAR=1 = serial, in order).
29+# Output is byte-identical at every value: each program's report
30+# is captured to its own file and printed in sorted order (as
31+# soon as it and all earlier ones are done), and the summary line
32+# and exit code are computed from the same per-program results.
33+# Each program holds one machine-wide slot (checks/sem.sh,
34+# LW_SLOTS, default 4) so concurrent runs by several agents queue
35+# instead of oversubscribing the machine.
36+set -uo pipefail
37+root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
38+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
39+export LG
40+update=0 both=0
41+dirs=()
42+for a in "$@"; do
43+ case $a in
44+ --both) both=1 ;;
45+ --update-expected) update=1 ;;
46+ -*) echo "unknown flag $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
47+ *) dirs+=("$a") ;;
48+ esac
49+done
50+[ ${#dirs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--both] [--update-expected] <dir>..." >&2; exit 2; }
51+
52+files=()
53+for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
54+ [ -d "$d" ] || { echo "no such dir: $d" >&2; exit 2; }
55+ # A SKIP file in the dir lists basenames to leave out (D15: div-* until Phase 2).
56+ skip=""; [ -f "$d/SKIP" ] && skip=$(sed -e 's/#.*//' "$d/SKIP" | tr '\n' ' ')
57+ while IFS= read -r f; do
58+ case " $skip " in *" $(basename "$f") "*) echo "SKIP $f"; continue;; esac
59+ files+=("$f")
60+ done < <(find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.lg' -o -name '*.clj' \) | LC_ALL=C sort)
61+done
62+[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "no programs in: ${dirs[*]}" >&2; exit 2; }
63+
64+if [ $update -eq 1 ]; then
65+ for f in "${files[@]}"; do
66+ case $f in */opmatrix/*) ;; *) [ -e "$f.expected" ] || continue ;; esac
67+ "$LG" "$f" >"$f.expected" 2>/dev/null || echo "warn: native lg exited $? on $f" >&2
68+ echo "wrote $f.expected"
69+ done
70+ exit 0
71+fi
72+
73+runner=$root/checks/wasm-run.sh
74+par=${LW_PAR:-3}
75+case $par in ''|*[!0-9]*|0) echo "LW_PAR must be a positive integer (got '$par')" >&2; exit 2;; esac
76+t=$(mktemp -d)
77+export t root both
78+xp=""
79+# stop a whole subtree (xargs -> sem.sh -> worker -> lg), parent first so xargs
80+# starts no replacement, so an interrupted run
81+# leaves no workers or held slots behind
82+killtree() { local c kids; kids=$(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null); kill "$1" 2>/dev/null; for c in $kids; do killtree "$c"; done; return 0; }
83+trap 'for c in $(pgrep -P $$ 2>/dev/null); do killtree "$c"; done; rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
84+trap 'exit 130' INT; trap 'exit 143' TERM HUP
85+
86+# The rtlib (src/.rtlib, or $LW_RTLIB_DIR) is built by the first driver run
87+# after a source change (45-175 s); N workers starting together would each
88+# build it (3 concurrent builds took 175 s against 45 s for one, identical
89+# output). So build it once, serially, before fanning out. A newer-than test
90+# on the cache file avoids an 8 s warm compile when nothing changed; a wrong
91+# guess costs only that compile or a redundant build, never a wrong result.
92+rtlib_warm() {
93+ [ "$par" -gt 1 ] && [ -x "$runner" ] || return 0
94+ local d=${LW_RTLIB_DIR:-$root/src/.rtlib} newest w
95+ newest=$(ls -t "$d"/rtlib-*.edn 2>/dev/null | head -1)
96+ if [ -n "$newest" ] && [ -z "$(find "$root/src" "$root/rt/wasm" -name '*.lg' -newer "$newest" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ]; then return 0; fi
97+ w=$(mktemp -d)
98+ # background + wait, so a TERM during the (long) build reaches the trap now, not after it
99+ "$root/checks/sem.sh" "$LG" -source-paths "$root/src" "$root/src/driver.lg" "$root/corpus/scalar/fib.clj" "$w/m.wat" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
100+ wait $!
101+ rm -rf "$w"
102+}
103+
104+# One program -> $t/<i>.line (its report line(s)) and $t/<i>.cls (match|hard|ni);
105+# $t/<i>.done is written last, so a reader that sees it sees both.
106+one() {
107+ local i=$1 f=$2 out cls w ns n nrc brc o rc
108+ out=$t/$i.line; cls=$t/$i.cls; w=$t/$i.w; mkdir -p "$w"
109+ if [ -e "$f.expected" ]; then
110+ "$LG" "$f" >"$w/native.out" 2>/dev/null
111+ if ! cmp -s "$f.expected" "$w/native.out"; then
112+ { echo "STALE-EXPECTED $f"; diff "$f.expected" "$w/native.out" | head -4 | sed 's/^/ /'; } >"$out"
113+ echo hard >"$cls"; : >"$t/$i.done"; return
114+ fi
115+ fi
116+ case $f in
117+ *_test.lg) if [ "$both" -eq 1 ]; then
118+ ns=$(sed -nE 's/^\(ns ([^ )]+).*/\1/p' "$f" | head -1)
119+ n=$(grep -c '^(deftest ' "$f")
120+ "$LG" -source-paths "$root/rt:$(dirname "$f")" "$root/checks/intrinsics-native-runner.lg" "$n" "$ns" >"$w/nat.out" 2>&1; nrc=$?
121+ "$root/checks/run-tests.sh" "$f" >"$w/bk.out" 2>&1; brc=$?
122+ if [ $nrc -eq 0 ] && [ $brc -eq 0 ]; then
123+ echo "MATCH $f ($(grep -m1 '^PASS' "$w/bk.out" | sed -E 's/^PASS [^ ]+ //'))" >"$out"; echo match >"$cls"
124+ else
125+ { echo "MISMATCH $f: native $([ $nrc -eq 0 ] && echo ok || grep -m1 'intrinsics-native' "$w/nat.out"), backend $([ $brc -eq 0 ] && echo ok || grep -m1 '^FAIL' "$w/bk.out" | sed -E 's/^FAIL [^ ]+ //')"
126+ grep -m1 '^ wasm' "$w/bk.out"; } >"$out"; echo hard >"$cls"
127+ fi
128+ : >"$t/$i.done"; return
129+ fi ;;
130+ esac
131+ if [ ! -x "$runner" ]; then
132+ echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED $f (checks/wasm-run.sh missing)" >"$out"; echo ni >"$cls"; : >"$t/$i.done"; return
133+ fi
134+ o=$(WASM_RUN=$runner "$root/checks/oracle.sh" "$f" 2>&1); rc=$?
135+ case $rc in
136+ 0) echo "MATCH $f" >"$out"; echo match >"$cls" ;;
137+ 2) echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED $f: $(printf '%s' "$o" | head -1)" >"$out"; echo ni >"$cls" ;;
138+ *) { echo "MISMATCH $f: $(printf '%s' "$o" | head -1)"
139+ printf '%s\n' "$o" | sed -n '2,6p' | sed 's/^/ /'; } >"$out"; echo hard >"$cls" ;;
140+ esac
141+ : >"$t/$i.done"
142+}
143+export -f one
144+export runner
145+
146+rtlib_warm
147+sem=$root/checks/sem.sh
148+match=0 hard=0 ni=0
149+# Print program i's captured report and fold its class into the summary.
150+emit() {
151+ local i=$1
152+ if [ -e "$t/$i.done" ]; then
153+ cat "$t/$i.line"
154+ case $(cat "$t/$i.cls") in match) match=$((match+1));; hard) hard=1;; ni) ni=1;; esac
155+ else
156+ echo "MISSING-RESULT ${files[$i]}"; hard=1
157+ fi
158+}
159+if [ "$par" -eq 1 ]; then
160+ for ((i=0; i<${#files[@]}; i++)); do "$sem" bash -c 'one "$1" "$2"' _ "$i" "${files[$i]}" & wait $!; emit "$i"; done
161+else
162+ for ((i=0; i<${#files[@]}; i++)); do printf '%s\0%s\0' "$i" "${files[$i]}"; done \
163+ | xargs -0 -n 2 -P "$par" "$sem" bash -c 'one "$1" "$2"' _ &
164+ xp=$!
165+ # in sorted order, as soon as each program and all before it are done
166+ for ((i=0; i<${#files[@]}; i++)); do
167+ while [ ! -e "$t/$i.done" ]; do
168+ kill -0 "$xp" 2>/dev/null || break
169+ sleep 0.2
170+ done
171+ emit "$i"
172+ done
173+ wait "$xp" 2>/dev/null; xp=""
174+fi
175+echo "$match/${#files[@]} MATCH"
176+[ $hard -eq 1 ] && exit 1
177+[ $match -eq ${#files[@]} ] && exit 0
178+exit 2
shell

2+# checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh — P2.1 native half: run the intrinsic and
3+# pvec test files under native lg with the reference wasm.intrinsics.
4+# Exit 0 iff every assertion passes AND the number of tests run equals the
5+# number of deftest forms in the files (guards the run-tests zero-suite trap).
6+# Tiers (D51): the default must finish under 90 s (68 s on 2026-10-01);
7+# SLOW=1 adds the 10k map/set builds, every map/set path at 1000 keys and
8+# the 1e6 reduce gate (3.5 min). Both tiers run every deftest, so the count
9+# guard holds in each; checks/gate.sh 2 sets SLOW=1.
10+# The eventual P2.1 check is `checks/run-corpus.sh corpus/intrinsics --both`.
11+#
12+# D106 (7): one lg process per *_test.lg file, LW_PAR at a time (default 4;
13+# LW_PAR=1 runs them one after another), each holding a machine-wide slot
14+# (checks/sem.sh) and loading the runtime itself (~2 s startup, accepted).
15+# The deftest-count guard runs per file (the runner exits 1 when its file
16+# registers a different number of tests than it has deftest forms) AND in
17+# total, and the last line is the same summary the one-process run printed:
18+# intrinsics-native: tests=N (expected N) pass=P fail=F error=E OK|FAILED
19+# with the counts summed over the files. Per-file output other than that
20+# summary (a failing test's report) is printed in file order before the
21+# one-process run's closing "Ran N tests containing M assertions." pair.
22+# Heaviest files start first (times measured 2026-10-01; files not listed
23+# default to light), because the run is bounded by the slowest file.

26+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}

32+expected=$(cat "${files[@]}" | grep -c '^(deftest ')
33+echo "tier: $([ "${SLOW:-}" = 1 ] && echo slow || echo default)"
34+# stop a whole subtree (xargs -> sem.sh -> worker -> lg), parent first so xargs
35+# starts no replacement, so an interrupted run
36+# leaves no workers or held slots behind
37+killtree() { local c kids; kids=$(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null); kill "$1" 2>/dev/null; for c in $kids; do killtree "$c"; done; return 0; }
38+t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT

40+export t

45+ xsofy_natives_test*) echo 24 ;; pvec_test*|vkind_test*) echo 18 ;; str_test*) echo 11 ;; core_test*) echo 9 ;;
46+ *) echo 1 ;;
47+ esac

81+echo "$fail failures, $err errors."

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/run-review2.sh — item P2.10: the corpus/review2 runtime bugs stay fixed.
3+#
4+# 1. Every corpus/review2/bug-*.lg runs, and corpus/review2/selfcheck.lg (the
5+# repros' expressions as [native runtime] pairs, the native side a fresh
6+# run in the same lg process) prints MATCH for it. A repro listed in
7+# corpus/review2/known-diffs.txt may MISMATCH (printed DEFERRED).
8+# 2. FUZZ_SEEDS seeds (default 300, from FUZZ_FROM=1000) of fuzz.lg with
9+# FUZZ_NOFOUND=1 (its filters for the reported bugs off), through
10+# corpus/review2/fuzz-check.lg, in FUZZ_SHARDS parallel lg processes
11+# (default 6): every FAIL signature must be in known-diffs.txt.
12+# Exit 0 iff both hold. RT=<dir> points the runtime at another rt/ copy
13+# (the falsification run uses a scratch copy with a fix reverted).
14+set -uo pipefail
15+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
16+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
17+RT=${RT:-rt}
18+SEEDS=${FUZZ_SEEDS:-300}; FROM=${FUZZ_FROM:-1000}; SHARDS=${FUZZ_SHARDS:-6}
19+allow=corpus/review2/known-diffs.txt
20+allowed() { grep -v '^#' "$allow" | cut -f1 | grep -qxF -- "$1"; }
21+tmp=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/review2.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
22+fail=0
23+
24+echo "== repros (selfcheck, native lg in the same process)"
25+"$LG" -source-paths "$RT" corpus/review2/selfcheck.lg > "$tmp/self.out" 2>&1
26+for f in corpus/review2/bug-*.lg; do
27+ b=${f##*/}; id=${b:0:6} # bug-NN
28+ if ! "$LG" -source-paths "$RT" "$f" > "$tmp/$id.run" 2>&1; then
29+ echo "$b CRASH"; sed 's/^/ /' "$tmp/$id.run" | head -5; fail=1; continue
30+ fi
31+ line=$(grep "^$id " "$tmp/self.out")
32+ case "$line" in
33+ "$id MATCH"*) echo "$b MATCH" ;;
34+ "$id MISMATCH"*) if allowed "$id"; then echo "$b DEFERRED (known-diffs.txt)"; else echo "$b MISMATCH"; fail=1; fi
35+ awk -v id="$id" '$0 ~ "^"id" " {p=1; next} /^bug-/ {p=0} p' "$tmp/self.out" ;;
36+ *) echo "$b NO SELFCHECK ENTRY"; fail=1 ;;

38+done

42+per=$(( (SEEDS + SHARDS - 1) / SHARDS )); pids=()
43+for ((k = 0; k < SHARDS; k++)); do
44+ a=$((FROM + k * per)); z=$((a + per)); [ "$z" -gt $((FROM + SEEDS)) ] && z=$((FROM + SEEDS)); [ "$a" -ge "$z" ] && continue

46+ "$LG" -source-paths "$RT" corpus/review2/fuzz.lg --eval corpus/review2/fuzz-check.lg > "$tmp/fuzz$k.out" 2>&1 &
47+ pids+=($!)
48+done
49+for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p"; done
50+done_n=$(cat "$tmp"/fuzz*.out | grep -c '^DONE')
51+[ "$done_n" -eq "${#pids[@]}" ] || { echo "fuzz: $done_n of ${#pids[@]} shards finished"; tail -5 "$tmp"/fuzz*.out; fail=1; }
52+grep -h 'sig=' "$tmp"/fuzz*.out | sed 's/.*sig=\(\[[^]]*\]\).*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c > "$tmp/sigs"
53+while read -r n sig; do
54+ if allowed "$sig"; then echo " allowed $n x $sig"; else echo " NEW $n x $sig"; fail=1
55+ grep -h -m1 -F "sig=$sig" "$tmp"/fuzz*.out | cut -c1-400 | sed 's/^/ /'; fi
56+done < "$tmp/sigs"
57+[ -s "$tmp/sigs" ] || echo " no FAIL signatures"
58+[ "$fail" = 0 ] && echo "run-review2: OK" || echo "run-review2: FAILED"
59+exit "$fail"

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/run.sh <item-id> — run one item's check from items.tsv. Exit 0 =
3+# that item is done; 1 = failing; 2 = the check script itself does not exist
4+# yet (the implementer builds the check with the feature; the reviewer runs
5+# this, never the implementer's own ad-hoc command).

10+[ -n "$line" ] || { echo "unknown item $id"; exit 2; }
11+cmd=$(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -f3)
12+echo "== $id: $(printf '%s' "$line" | cut -f4)"
13+echo "-- $cmd"
14+set -- $cmd
15+# a shell builtin (e.g. the P1.0 row's leading `test -x`) is a real command too
16+case "$(type -t "$1" 2>/dev/null)" in file|builtin) ;; *) [ -x "$1" ] || { echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED: $1 missing"; exit 2; } ;; esac
17+eval "$cmd"

@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/sem.sh <cmd...> — run <cmd> holding one of N machine-wide slots.
3+#
4+# The laptop has 8 cores (4 performance). Measured 2026-10-01: the same
5+# check (checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh, default tier) takes 90 s at load
6+# 10 and 525 s at load 29-47, and the oracle compile of one program goes
7+# from 8 s to 30 s. Three agents each running a serial gate already
8+# oversubscribe the machine; a parallel gate per agent would make it worse.
9+# So parallelism is granted by ONE pool shared by every agent and every
10+# script, not per script: LW_SLOTS (default 4) tokens in $LW_SEM
11+# (default ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-sem: per-user on macOS, outside any watched or
12+# per-session tree; set LW_SEM to one path if agents' TMPDIRs differ).
13+#
14+# mkdir is the atomic primitive (no flock on macOS bash 3). A slot is a
15+# directory holding the holder's pid; a slot whose pid is dead is reclaimed
16+# (by an atomic rename, so two reclaimers cannot both delete a slot that a
17+# third has just taken), so a killed agent cannot wedge the pool. Wait is a
18+# 0.5 s poll, bounded by LW_SEM_WAIT (default 1800 s), after which the command
19+# runs anyway with a warning (never silently deadlock a gate).
20+#
21+# Wrap LEAVES (one oracle program, one census shard, one native test file),
22+# never an orchestrator that itself fans out through the pool: a gate holding
23+# a slot per row while its rows wait for slots can deadlock four agents'
24+# gates against each other. As a backstop a command started under a held slot
25+# sees LW_SEM_HELD=1 and runs without taking another, so accidental nesting
26+# costs oversubscription, not a deadlock.
27+set -uo pipefail
28+if [ -n "${LW_SEM_HELD:-}" ]; then exec "$@"; fi
29+n=${LW_SLOTS:-4}; d=${LW_SEM:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-sem}; d=${d%/}; mkdir -p "$d"
30+deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + ${LW_SEM_WAIT:-1800} ))
31+got=""
32+# a slot whose holder died, or that never recorded a pid (killed between
33+# mkdir and the write; older than 5 s so a live acquirer is not mistaken)
34+reclaim() {
35+ local s=$1 p dead=$1.dead.$$
36+ p=$(cat "$s/pid" 2>/dev/null)
37+ if [ -n "$p" ]; then kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null && return; else
38+ [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$s" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) )) -gt 5 ] || return
39+ fi
40+ command mv "$s" "$dead" 2>/dev/null || return
41+ # re-check what we actually moved: another reclaimer may have refilled the slot
42+ p=$(cat "$dead/pid" 2>/dev/null)
43+ if [ -n "$p" ] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; then command mv "$dead" "$s" 2>/dev/null || true; return; fi
44+ rm -rf "$dead"
45+}
46+while :; do
47+ for ((i=0;i<n;i++)); do
48+ s=$d/slot$i
49+ if mkdir "$s" 2>/dev/null; then echo $$ > "$s/pid"; got=$s; break; fi
50+ reclaim "$s"
51+ done
52+ [ -n "$got" ] && break
53+ if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then echo "sem: waited ${LW_SEM_WAIT:-1800}s, running unslotted" >&2; break; fi
54+ sleep 0.5
55+done
56+trap '[ -n "$got" ] && rm -rf "$got"' EXIT
57+trap 'exit 130' INT; trap 'exit 143' TERM HUP
58+LW_SEM_HELD=1 "$@"
59+exit $?
shell

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/size-boot.sh — P4.3: bundle size and boot time of the emitted lane
3+# (lane 5) against the stock-Go lane, measured now on this machine, and the
4+# TinyGo lane's recorded figures (memory letgo-aot-tinygo-xsofy-lanes,
5+# 2026-09-20, xsofy 0e2a8b8 × let-go 36b13f79: 2.3 MB, 8725 ms to title,
6+# 12553 ms to the game screen; not rebuilt here, TinyGo 0.42 + let-go#939).
7+#
8+# Bundle = every file the page fetches: stock = index.html (the wasm inline,
9+# base64 of gzip, as `lg -w` emits it) + coi-serviceworker.js; lw = index.html
10+# (the same shell injected) + xsofy-shell-adapter.js + lg-wasm-host.js +
11+# module.wasm. Sizes raw, brotli -q 11 and gzip -9 (GitHub Pages serves gzip
12+# only). Boot = local-scripts/browser-smoke-playwright/zz-boot-time-probe.mjs
13+# (navigation to "press any key", then Space to the HUD), REPS runs per lane
14+# (default 5), medians. Both lanes are built by checks/lane5.sh's caches
15+# (run it first, or this script builds them the same way).
16+# Writes the table to corpus/xsofy/size-boot.md and prints it.
17+# Exit 0 iff both lanes boot to the map in every run and the table is written.

19+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
20+ws=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
21+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
22+XSOFY=${XSOFY:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/xsofy}
23+REPS=${REPS:-5}
24+pw=$ws/local-scripts/browser-smoke-playwright
25+t=$(mktemp -d); trap '[ -n "${KEEP:-}" ] && echo "kept $t" >&2 || rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
26+
27+# the stock lane: lane5.sh's cache (same key), built by lane5.sh if missing
28+cache=${LW_LANE5_CACHE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-lane5-stock}
29+key=$( { echo 4e769212; shasum "$LG"; cat "$XSOFY/main.lg" "$XSOFY/tools/xsofy-shell.html";
30+ find "$XSOFY/xsofy" -name '*.lg' -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 cat; } | md5 -q)
31+stock=$cache/$key
32+if [ ! -f "$stock/index.html" ]; then
33+ echo "stock lane not cached: running checks/lane5.sh to build it" >&2
34+ "$here/checks/lane5.sh" >"$t/lane5.log" 2>&1
35+ [ -f "$stock/index.html" ] || { echo "FAIL: no stock lane"; cat "$t/lane5.log"; exit 1; }
36+fi
37+"$here/host/build-xsofy-module.sh" "$t/module.wasm" 2>"$t/mod.log" || { cat "$t/mod.log"; echo "FAIL: module"; exit 1; }
38+"$here/host/build-xsofy-serve.sh" "$t/lw" "$t/module.wasm" || exit 1
39+raw_module=$(sed -n 's/^module: \([0-9]*\) bytes raw.*/\1/p' "$t/mod.log")
40+
41+sizes() { # sizes <file...> -> "raw brotli gzip" summed
42+ local r=0 b=0 g=0 f
43+ for f in "$@"; do
44+ r=$((r + $(wc -c <"$f"))); b=$((b + $(brotli -c -q 11 "$f" | wc -c))); g=$((g + $(gzip -9 -c "$f" | wc -c)))

46+ echo "$r $b $g"

48+read -r s_raw s_br s_gz <<<"$(sizes "$stock/index.html" "$stock/coi-serviceworker.js")"
49+read -r l_raw l_br l_gz <<<"$(sizes "$t/lw/index.html" "$t/lw/xsofy-shell-adapter.js" "$t/lw/lg-wasm-host.js" "$t/lw/module.wasm")"

51+
52+free_port() { python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])'; }
53+(cd "$pw" && node zz-boot-time-probe.mjs "$stock" "$(free_port)" stock "$REPS") >"$t/boot-stock.json" 2>&1

55+
56+python3 - "$t" "$here/corpus/xsofy/size-boot.md" "$s_raw" "$s_br" "$s_gz" "$l_raw" "$l_br" "$l_gz" "$m_raw" "$m_br" "$m_gz" "$raw_module" "$REPS" <<'EOF'
57+import json, sys, datetime, subprocess
58+t, md = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
59+s_raw, s_br, s_gz, l_raw, l_br, l_gz, m_raw, m_br, m_gz, raw_module, reps = map(int, sys.argv[3:14])
60+def load(f):
61+ try: return json.loads(open(f'{t}/{f}').read().strip().splitlines()[-1])
62+ except Exception as e: return {'failure': f'{f}: {e}'}
63+bs, bl = load('boot-stock.json'), load('boot-lw.json')
64+ok = all('titleMedian' in b and len(b.get('screenMs', [])) == reps for b in (bs, bl))
65+mb = lambda n: f'{n/1e6:.2f} MB' if n >= 1e6 else f'{n/1e3:.0f} KB'
66+ms = lambda b, k: f"{b[k]} ms" if k in b else 'FAIL'
67+xs = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', __import__('os').path.expanduser('~/projects-new/3p/xsofy'), 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'],
68+ capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
69+today = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
70+rows = [
71+ ('lane 5: lower-wasm (emitted)', mb(l_raw), mb(l_br), mb(l_gz), ms(bl, 'titleMedian'), ms(bl, 'screenMedian')),
72+ ('stock Go (lg -w, let-go 4e769212)', mb(s_raw), mb(s_br), mb(s_gz), ms(bs, 'titleMedian'), ms(bs, 'screenMedian')),
73+ ('TinyGo (recorded 2026-09-20, not re-run)', '2.3 MB', '1.27 MB (floor build)', '1.70 MB (floor build)', '8725 ms', '12553 ms'),
74+]
75+out = [f'# P4.3: lane 5 size and boot (measured {today}, checks/size-boot.sh)', '',
76+ f'xsofy {xs}, lg 4e769212 (`lg-4e76921230`), headless Chromium via zz-boot-time-probe.mjs, {reps} runs per lane, medians.',
77+ 'Bundle = every file the page fetches (shell included in both). Boot times are from navigation; the title card itself',
78+ 'animates for part of the time-to-title on every lane.', '',
79+ '| lane | bundle raw | brotli -q 11 | gzip -9 | time-to-title | time-to-map |', '|---|---|---|---|---|---|']
80+out += ['| ' + ' | '.join(r) + ' |' for r in rows]
81+out += ['', f'Lane 5 module alone: {raw_module:,} B as emitted, {m_raw:,} B after `wasm-opt -O3` (served), '
82+ f'{m_br:,} B brotli, {m_gz:,} B gzip.',
83+ f"Runs (ms): lane 5 title {bl.get('titleMs')}, map {bl.get('screenMs')}; stock title {bs.get('titleMs')}, map {bs.get('screenMs')}.",
84+ 'TinyGo row: memory `letgo-aot-tinygo-xsofy-lanes` (xsofy 0e2a8b8 × let-go 36b13f79, another day and load); its 2.3 MB is',

86+for b in (bs, bl):

88+text = '\n'.join(out) + '\n'
89+open(md, 'w').write(text)
90+print(text)
91+sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
92+EOF

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/wasm-hash.sh <edn> <kind> — the P2.2 hook (D18): print the decimal
3+# uint32 hash the BACKEND computes for (read-string edn), kind "pvector" via
4+# with-meta (D79: always PersistentVector). Prints LIMIT for a row whose
5+# read-string is a named limit in the runtime (bigint/ratio/bigdec, D15).
6+#
7+# Compiling one module per row would cost ~10 s × 201, so the hook batches:
8+# on first use it emits ONE program covering every row of vectors.tsv, runs it
9+# through checks/wasm-run.sh, caches the answers keyed by the table + tree
10+# hash, and answers each call from the cache.
11+set -uo pipefail
12+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
13+edn=$1; kind=${2:-}
14+tsv=corpus/hash/vectors.tsv
15+key=$( (cat "$tsv"; cat src/*.lg rt/wasm/*.lg) | md5 -q)
16+cache=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-wasm-hash-$key.tsv
17+if [ ! -s "$cache" ]; then
18+ prog=$(mktemp -d)/hashes.lg
19+ python3 - "$tsv" > "$prog" <<'PY'
20+import sys
21+rows=[l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(sys.argv[1]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
22+def lit(s): return '"'+s.replace("\\","\\\\").replace('"','\\"')+'"'
23+print("(def rows [")
24+for i,(kind,edn,_h) in enumerate(rows):
25+ print(f" [{i} {lit(kind)} {lit(edn)}]")
26+print("])")
27+print('''(doseq [[i kind edn] rows]
28+ (let [r (try (let [v (read-string edn)
29+ v (if (= kind "pvector") (with-meta v {:pv true}) v)]
30+ (str (hash v)))
31+ (catch Exception e (if (clojure.string/includes? (str (ex-message e)) "lower-wasm:") "LIMIT" (str "ERR " (ex-message e)))))]
32+ (println (str i "\\t" kind "\\t" r))))''')
33+PY
34+ checks/sem.sh checks/wasm-run.sh "$prog" > "$cache.tmp" 2>"$cache.err" && command mv "$cache.tmp" "$cache" || { echo "ERR compile/run failed: $(head -1 "$cache.err")"; exit 1; }
35+fi
36+python3 - "$tsv" "$cache" "$edn" "$kind" <<'PY'
37+import sys
38+tsv,cache,edn,kind=sys.argv[1:]
39+rows=[l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(tsv) if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
40+ans={l.split("\t")[0]:l.rstrip("\n").split("\t")[2] for l in open(cache) if "\t" in l}
41+for i,(k,e,_h) in enumerate(rows):
42+ if k==kind and e==edn:
43+ print(ans.get(str(i),"ERR missing")); sys.exit(0)
44+print("ERR row not in table"); sys.exit(1)
45+PY
shell

@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/wasm-run.sh <prog.lg> [args...] — compile a program through the
3+# lower-wasm backend and run it under node, behaving like `lg <prog.lg> args`
4+# on stdout and exit status (DECISIONS D12). This is oracle.sh's WASM_RUN.
5+#
6+# A compile failure (driver error, unsupported op, invalid WAT) exits 1 with
7+# the tool output on stderr, so the oracle reports it as a MISMATCH rather
8+# than a match.
9+#
10+# Env: LG (default the plan's pinned main build), KEEP=1, LG_ARGS (the same
11+# native-lg args oracle.sh passes; its `-source-paths <dirs>` names the
12+# library roots a multi-namespace program requires from, P3.2),
13+# LW_MODULE_CACHE=<dir> (reuse the compiled module of an unchanged program:
14+# keyed by the program, its source roots, src/ and rt/; args are run-time).
15+set -uo pipefail
16+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
17+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
18+prog=${1:?usage: wasm-run.sh <prog.lg> [args...]}; shift
19+sp=""
20+read -r -a lgargs <<<"${LG_ARGS:-}"
21+for ((i = 0; i < ${#lgargs[@]}; i++)); do
22+ [ "${lgargs[$i]}" = -source-paths ] && sp=${lgargs[$((i + 1))]:-}
23+done
24+t=$(mktemp -d); trap '[ -n "${KEEP:-}" ] && echo "kept $t" >&2 || rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
25+drv=("$LG" -source-paths "$here/src${sp:+:$sp}" "$here/src/driver.lg")
26+[ -n "$sp" ] && drv+=(-source-paths "$sp")
27+key=""
28+if [ -n "${LW_MODULE_CACHE:-}" ]; then
29+ mkdir -p "$LW_MODULE_CACHE"
30+ key=$( { cat "$prog"; echo "$sp"; cat "$here"/src/*.lg "$here"/src/*.mjs "${LW_RT_DIR:-$here/rt/wasm}"/*.lg;
31+ [ -n "$sp" ] && IFS=: read -r -a roots <<<"$sp" && for r in "${roots[@]}"; do find "$r" -name '*.lg' -not -path '*/worktrees/*' -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 cat; done; } | md5 -q)
32+fi
33+if [ -n "$key" ] && [ -f "$LW_MODULE_CACHE/$key.wasm" ]; then
34+ cp "$LW_MODULE_CACHE/$key.wasm" "$t/m.wasm"
35+else
36+ if ! "${drv[@]}" "$prog" "$t/m.wat" >"$t/drv.log" 2>&1; then
37+ cat "$t/drv.log" >&2; exit 1
38+ fi
39+ wasm-tools parse "$t/m.wat" -o "$t/m.wasm" || exit 1
40+ [ -n "$key" ] && command cp "$t/m.wasm" "$LW_MODULE_CACHE/$key.wasm.tmp$$" && command mv -f "$LW_MODULE_CACHE/$key.wasm.tmp$$" "$LW_MODULE_CACHE/$key.wasm"
41+fi
42+node "$here/src/run.mjs" "$t/m.wasm" "$prog" "$@"
shell

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# checks/world-parity.sh [--keys wait|autoex|descend|deep|<string>] [N] [turns]
3+# Phase 3 oracle: corpus/dump-world.lg must print identical bytes under native
4+# lg and under the backend for seeds 1..N. Native side needs xsofy on the
5+# source path; the backend side is checks/wasm-run.sh, which reads the same
6+# -source-paths from LG_ARGS (P3.2). --keys picks the keystroke fixture
7+# (corpus/depth/measure.lg's shapes: autoex = "x" then waits, descend = ">"
8+# then waits; neither leaves floor 1 in 200 turns, since ">" only routes to
9+# stairs already seen). deep = 98 autoexplore steps then ">" each turn, which
10+# descends to floor 2 on seeds 7, 9 and 10 by turn ~130 (native, 2026-10-01).
11+# Any other value is passed through as dump-world's keys string.
12+# SEEDS="7 9 10" replaces 1..N.
13+# The module is compiled once and reused across seeds (LW_MODULE_CACHE).
14+# Prints one line per seed, the module size, and "n/N MATCH"; exit 0 iff all
15+# MATCH, 2 if the backend runner is missing.
16+set -uo pipefail
17+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
18+KEYS=wait
19+if [ "${1:-}" = --keys ]; then KEYS=$2; shift 2; fi
20+N=${1:-20}; TURNS=${2:-60}
21+XSOFY=${XSOFY:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/xsofy}
22+[ -x checks/wasm-run.sh ] || { echo "NOT IMPLEMENTED: checks/wasm-run.sh missing"; exit 2; }
23+dots=$(printf '%*s' "$TURNS" '' | tr ' ' .)
24+case "$KEYS" in
25+ wait) keys=. ;;
26+ autoex) keys="x${dots:1}" ;;
27+ descend) keys=">${dots:1}" ;;
28+ deep) keys="$(printf '%98s' '' | tr ' ' x)$(printf '%*s' "$TURNS" '' | tr ' ' '>')" ;;
29+ *) keys=$KEYS ;;
30+esac
31+cache=${LW_MODULE_CACHE:-$(mktemp -d)}
32+[ -n "${LW_MODULE_CACHE:-}" ] || trap 'rm -rf "$cache"' EXIT
33+export LW_MODULE_CACHE=$cache
34+ok=0
35+seeds=${SEEDS:-$(seq 1 "$N")}
36+N=$(wc -w <<<"$seeds" | tr -d ' ')
37+for seed in $seeds; do
38+ r=$(LG_ARGS="-source-paths $XSOFY" XSOFY_ROOT="$XSOFY" WASM_RUN=checks/wasm-run.sh checks/oracle.sh corpus/dump-world.lg "$seed" "$TURNS" "$keys" 2>&1)
39+ printf '%-16s seed %s\n' "$(head -1 <<<"$r")" "$seed"
40+ [ "$(head -1 <<<"$r")" = MATCH ] && ok=$((ok+1))
41+ [ "$(head -1 <<<"$r")" = MATCH ] || sed -n '2,4p' <<<"$r" | cut -c1-300
42+done
43+# the module this run used: the newest in the cache
44+m=""; for f in "$cache"/*.wasm; do [ -f "$f" ] && { [ -z "$m" ] || [ "$f" -nt "$m" ]; } && m=$f; done
45+if [ -n "$m" ]; then
46+ opt=$(/opt/homebrew/opt/binaryen/bin/wasm-opt -O3 --enable-gc --enable-reference-types --enable-exception-handling \
47+ --enable-bulk-memory --enable-tail-call --enable-multivalue "$m" -o - 2>/dev/null | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
48+ echo "module: $(wc -c <"$m" | tr -d ' ') bytes raw, $opt bytes after wasm-opt -O3"
49+fi
50+echo "$ok/$N MATCH (keys=$KEYS, turns=$TURNS)"
51+[ "$ok" -eq "$N" ]
shell

1+#!/usr/bin/env bash
2+# host/build-xsofy-module.sh <out.wasm> — xsofy's real entry (main.lg)
3+# compiled by the backend (P4.1), then wasm-opt -O3: the module the browser
4+# lane serves as module.wasm. Shared by checks/browser-boot.sh --xsofy,
5+# checks/lane5.sh and checks/size-boot.sh.
6+#
7+# Cached: the compile takes ~80 s, so the result is kept under
8+# $LW_XSOFY_CACHE (default ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-xsofy-module) keyed by an md5
9+# of everything that can change it: the lg binary, src/, the runtime sources
10+# (LW_RT_DIR when set, D104), xsofy's sources and wasm-opt's flags.
11+# Prints "cache hit|built <key>" and the raw/optimised sizes on stderr.
12+# Env: LG, XSOFY, LW_RT_DIR, LW_NO_OPT=1 (serve the unoptimised module),
13+# LW_XSOFY_RAW=<path> (also copy the unoptimised module there).
14+set -euo pipefail
15+here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
16+out=${1:?usage: build-xsofy-module.sh <out.wasm>}
17+LG=${LG:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230}
18+XSOFY=${XSOFY:-$HOME/projects-new/3p/xsofy}
19+OPT=/opt/homebrew/opt/binaryen/bin/wasm-opt
20+optflags=(-O3 --enable-gc --enable-reference-types --enable-exception-handling --enable-bulk-memory
21+ --enable-tail-call --enable-multivalue)
22+cache=${LW_XSOFY_CACHE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-xsofy-module}; mkdir -p "$cache"
23+key=$( { shasum "$LG"; echo "${optflags[*]} ${LW_NO_OPT:-}";
24+ cat "$here"/src/*.lg "${LW_RT_DIR:-$here/rt/wasm}"/*.lg "${LW_RT_DIR:-$here/rt/wasm}"/README.md;
25+ cat "$XSOFY/main.lg"; find "$XSOFY/xsofy" -name '*.lg' -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 cat; } | md5 -q)
26+if [ -f "$cache/$key.wasm" ]; then
27+ echo "cache hit $key" >&2
28+else
29+ t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
30+ if ! "$here/checks/sem.sh" "$LG" -source-paths "$here/src:$XSOFY" "$here/src/driver.lg" \
31+ -source-paths "$XSOFY" "$XSOFY/main.lg" "$t/m.wat" >"$t/drv.log" 2>&1; then
32+ grep -v 'catalog' "$t/drv.log" >&2; exit 1
33+ fi
34+ wasm-tools parse "$t/m.wat" -o "$t/raw.wasm"
35+ if [ -n "${LW_NO_OPT:-}" ]; then command cp "$t/raw.wasm" "$t/m.wasm"; else "$OPT" "${optflags[@]}" "$t/raw.wasm" -o "$t/m.wasm"; fi
36+ command cp "$t/raw.wasm" "$cache/$key.raw.wasm"
37+ command cp "$t/m.wasm" "$cache/$key.wasm.tmp$$" && command mv -f "$cache/$key.wasm.tmp$$" "$cache/$key.wasm"
38+ echo "built $key" >&2
39+fi
40+command cp "$cache/$key.wasm" "$out"
41+[ -n "${LW_XSOFY_RAW:-}" ] && command cp "$cache/$key.raw.wasm" "$LW_XSOFY_RAW"
42+echo "module: $(wc -c <"$cache/$key.raw.wasm" | tr -d ' ') bytes raw, $(wc -c <"$out" | tr -d ' ') bytes served" >&2

1+<!doctype html>
2+<!-- Minimal host page for lower-wasm modules (P4.0). Not the game shell:
3+ P4.1 swaps this page's <pre> "shell" for xsofy/tools/xsofy-shell.html,
4+ which binds only through window.LetGoHost, so the surface below keeps
5+ let-go's shape (onReady / onOutput / onEmit / sendInput / setSize).
6+ ?module=<url> picks the .wasm (default module.wasm). -->
7+<html lang="en">
8+<head>
9+<meta charset="utf-8">
10+<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
11+<title>lower-wasm host</title>
12+<style>
13+ :root { --bg: #0a0e14; --fg: #d4c5a0; --dim: #6b7280; }
14+ body { margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); font: 14px/1.4 ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; }
15+ #status { color: var(--dim); margin-bottom: 8px; }
16+ #out { margin: 0; white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-all; outline: none; }
17+ .err { color: #ff6b6b; }
18+</style>
19+</head>
20+<body>
21+<div id="status">loading…</div>
22+<pre id="out" tabindex="0"></pre>
23+<script>
24+// window.LetGoHost — defined by a classic script before any shell code, as
25+// let-go's lg-host-core.js is, so a shell can bind at parse time. Output and
26+// the ready signal are buffered until the shell registers.
27+window.LetGoHost = (function () {
28+ let outputSink = null; const outputBuffer = [];
29+ let readyCb = null, readyMode = null;
30+ let emitSink = (name, data) => window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(name, { detail: data }));
31+ return {
32+ onReady(cb) { readyCb = cb; if (readyMode !== null) cb(readyMode); },
33+ onOutput(cb) { outputSink = cb; for (const s of outputBuffer.splice(0)) cb(s); },
34+ onEmit(cb) { emitSink = cb; },
35+ sendInput(s) { return window._lgwHost ? window._lgwHost.sendInput(s) : false; },
36+ setSize(c, r) { if (window._lgwHost) window._lgwHost.setSize(c, r); },
37+ _output(s) { if (outputSink) outputSink(s); else outputBuffer.push(s); },
38+ _emit(name, data) { emitSink(name, data); },
39+ _ready(mode) { readyMode = mode; if (readyCb) readyCb(mode); },
40+ };
41+})();
42+</script>
43+<script>
44+// This page's own stand-in shell: a <pre> and a keydown listener.
45+(function () {
46+ const out = document.getElementById('out');
47+ const KEYS = { Enter: '\r', Escape: '\x1b', Backspace: '\x7f', Tab: '\t',

27+ && typeof WebAssembly.Suspending === 'function' && typeof WebAssembly.promising === 'function';

35+ onEmit = () => {}, urlParams = null, argv = ['lg'] } = {}) {

37+ this.onOutput = onOutput;
38+ this.onEmit = onEmit; // (name, dataJson) for js/emit

47+ this.running = false;
48+ // one streaming decoder per fd so a UTF-8 sequence split across two
49+ // writes still decodes

51+ this.mem = null;

60+ if (this.keys.length >= this.keyCapacity) return false;

1+// node-host.mjs — lg-wasm-host.js under Node, for CI and for the three-host
2+// matrix in checks/browser-boot.sh.
3+//
4+// node host/node-host.mjs <module.wasm> [--keys abq] [--env K=V ...] [--size 100x30] [--coalesce]
5+//
6+// Keys: each character of --keys is one key, sent once the module is
7+// running, then end of input; otherwise piped stdin feeds keys one character
8+// at a time (EOF = end of input, read-key → nil), and a TTY stdin goes raw
9+// (one keypress = one key). stdout/stderr and the exit code behave like
10+// src/run.mjs. LG_HOST_TIMING=1 adds a timing line on stderr.
11+//
12+// Coalescing (D98) is OFF here unless --coalesce is given: scripted and piped
13+// input should reach the program key for key ("jjj" is three reads), which is
14+// what this host did before D98. The browser host coalesces by default.
15+//
16+// Stack depth: under JSPI `lw main` runs on a V8 secondary stack whose size
17+// is --wasm-stack-switching-stack-size (default 984 kB, ~5-10k lg frames)
18+// and whose limit check also honours --stack-size. A worker's
19+// resourceLimits.stackSizeMb (run.mjs, D33) does not reach that stack, so
20+// this host runs on the main thread and re-execs node with both flags when
21+// they are missing; 256 MB matches run.mjs (1M-deep int recursion passes).
22+import fs from 'node:fs';
23+import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
24+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
25+
26+const FLAGS = ['--stack-size=262000', '--wasm-stack-switching-stack-size=262144'];
27+if (!process.execArgv.some((a) => a.startsWith('--wasm-stack-switching-stack-size'))) {
28+ const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [...FLAGS, fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), ...process.argv.slice(2)], { stdio: 'inherit' });
29+ process.exit(r.status ?? 1);
30+}
31+
32+const { LgWasmHost } = await import('./lg-wasm-host.js');
33+const args = process.argv.slice(2);
34+const opts = { wasm: null, keys: null, env: {}, cols: 80, rows: 24, coalesce: false };
35+for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
36+ const a = args[i];
37+ if (a === '--keys') opts.keys = args[++i];
38+ else if (a === '--env') { const [k, ...v] = args[++i].split('='); opts.env[k] = v.join('='); }
39+ else if (a === '--coalesce') opts.coalesce = true;
40+ else if (a === '--size') { const [c, r] = args[++i].split('x').map(Number); opts.cols = c; opts.rows = r; }
41+ else opts.wasm = a;
42+}
43+if (!opts.wasm) { console.error('usage: node-host.mjs <module.wasm> [--keys STR] [--env K=V] [--size CxR]'); process.exit(2); }
44+
45+const host = new LgWasmHost({
46+ env: opts.env, cols: opts.cols, rows: opts.rows,
47+ // piped/--keys input arrives faster than a human types; queue all of it
48+ keyCapacity: Infinity,
49+ coalesceKeys: opts.coalesce,
50+ onOutput: (text, fd) => fs.writeSync(fd === 2 ? 2 : 1, text),
51+});
52+const done = host.run(fs.readFileSync(opts.wasm));

54+// dropped, as in let-go); run() sets `running` just before entering lw main

57+ if (!host.running) return setTimeout(feed, 1);
58+ if (opts.keys !== null) {
59+ for (const ch of opts.keys) host.sendInput(ch);
60+ host.closeInput();

64+ process.stdin.on('data', (d) => { if (d[0] === 3) { process.stdin.setRawMode(false); process.exit(130); } host.sendInput(d.toString('utf8')); });

1+#!/usr/bin/env python3
2+# host/pty-run.py <cols> <rows> <keys> <cmd...> — run cmd on a pseudo-terminal
3+# of that size (TIOCSWINSZ), the way native lg's term/* natives need one
4+# (term/size is nil and read-key cannot go raw off a TTY), send each char of
5+# <keys> as one keypress once output has been quiet for 0.3 s, and write
6+# everything the program printed to stdout, raw. The native side of
7+# corpus/host/term-demo.lg's comparison with host/node-host.mjs (P4.1).
8+# Exits with the program's status (124 if it had to be killed).
9+import os, pty, sys, struct, fcntl, termios, time, select
10+cols, rows, keys = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
11+pid, fd = pty.fork()
12+if pid == 0:
13+ os.execvp(sys.argv[4], sys.argv[4:])
14+fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
15+out = bytearray()
16+def pump(quiet, limit=10.0):
17+ """read until `quiet` s pass with no output (or EOF / limit); False at EOF"""
18+ end, last = time.time() + limit, time.time()
19+ while time.time() < end and time.time() - last < quiet:
20+ r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.02)
21+ if r:
22+ try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
23+ except OSError: return False
24+ if not d: return False
25+ out.extend(d); last = time.time()
26+ return True
27+alive = pump(0.5)
28+for k in keys:
29+ if not alive: break
30+ os.write(fd, k.encode()); alive = pump(0.3)

34+ p, st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)

37+else:
38+ os.kill(pid, 9); os.waitpid(pid, 0)
39+sys.stdout.buffer.write(bytes(out))

1+;; wasmtime-adapter.wat — the host/ABI.md imports implemented on WASI
2+;; preview1, for running a lower-wasm module under the wasmtime CLI. No JS
3+;; there, so no JSPI: sleep and read_key simply block the thread.
4+;;
5+;; checks/browser-boot.sh merges it into the program with binaryen, once as
6+;; "env" and once (minus the "memory" export) as "term":
7+;; wasm-merge --rename-export-conflicts prog.wasm main a.wasm env a-term.wasm term
8+;; The adapter works on the program's memory, which it imports as
9+;; main."lw mem" and re-exports as "memory" because WASI needs that name.
10+;;
11+;; Scratch: the low addresses are NOT free (the backend keeps an active data
12+;; segment at 0, "niltruefalse…", and print_str reads it from there), and
13+;; 32.. is where it copies strings for env.write. The adapter's iovecs,
14+;; digits and poll structs therefore live in the top 128 bytes of memory; if
15+;; the string being written reaches into them, the adapter grows memory by a
16+;; page first. The program checks memory.size before every copy, so a grow
17+;; here only gives it room.
18+(module
19+ (import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "fd_write" (func $fd_write (param i32 i32 i32 i32) (result i32)))
20+ (import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "fd_read" (func $fd_read (param i32 i32 i32 i32) (result i32)))
21+ (import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "poll_oneoff" (func $poll_oneoff (param i32 i32 i32 i32) (result i32)))
22+ (import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "clock_time_get" (func $clock_time_get (param i32 i64 i32) (result i32)))
23+ (import "main" "lw mem" (memory 1))
24+ (export "memory" (memory 0))
25+ ;; base of a 128-byte scratch area that does not overlap [0, live_end)
26+ (func $scratch (param $live_end i32) (result i32) (local $base i32)
27+ (local.set $base (i32.sub (i32.mul (memory.size) (i32.const 65536)) (i32.const 128)))
28+ (if (i32.gt_u (local.get $live_end) (local.get $base))
29+ (then (drop (memory.grow (i32.const 1)))
30+ (local.set $base (i32.sub (i32.mul (memory.size) (i32.const 65536)) (i32.const 128)))))
31+ (local.get $base))
32+ (func $out (param $fd i32) (param $ptr i32) (param $len i32) (local $s i32)
33+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.add (local.get $ptr) (local.get $len))))
34+ (i32.store (local.get $s) (local.get $ptr))
35+ (i32.store offset=4 (local.get $s) (local.get $len))
36+ (drop (call $fd_write (local.get $fd) (local.get $s) (i32.const 1) (i32.add (local.get $s) (i32.const 8)))))
37+ (func (export "write") (param $fd i32) (param $ptr i32) (param $len i32) (result i32)
38+ (call $out (local.get $fd) (local.get $ptr) (local.get $len))
39+ (local.get $len))
40+ (func (export "print_str") (param $ptr i32) (param $len i32)
41+ (call $out (i32.const 1) (local.get $ptr) (local.get $len)))
42+ (func (export "print_nl") (local $s i32)
43+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.const 0)))
44+ (i32.store8 offset=64 (local.get $s) (i32.const 10))
45+ (call $out (i32.const 1) (i32.add (local.get $s) (i32.const 64)) (i32.const 1)))
46+ ;; digits right-aligned ending at s+96 (i64 min is 20 characters)
47+ (func (export "print_i64") (param $v i64) (local $s i32) (local $end i32) (local $p i32) (local $d i64) (local $neg i32)
48+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.const 0)))
49+ (local.set $end (i32.add (local.get $s) (i32.const 96)))
50+ (local.set $p (local.get $end))
51+ (local.set $neg (i64.lt_s (local.get $v) (i64.const 0)))
52+ (loop $l
53+ (local.set $d (i64.rem_s (local.get $v) (i64.const 10)))
54+ (if (local.get $neg) (then (local.set $d (i64.sub (i64.const 0) (local.get $d)))))
55+ (local.set $p (i32.sub (local.get $p) (i32.const 1)))
56+ (i32.store8 (local.get $p) (i32.add (i32.const 48) (i32.wrap_i64 (local.get $d))))
57+ (local.set $v (i64.div_s (local.get $v) (i64.const 10)))
58+ (br_if $l (i64.ne (local.get $v) (i64.const 0))))
59+ (if (local.get $neg) (then
60+ (local.set $p (i32.sub (local.get $p) (i32.const 1)))
61+ (i32.store8 (local.get $p) (i32.const 45))))
62+ (call $out (i32.const 1) (local.get $p) (i32.sub (local.get $end) (local.get $p))))
63+ (func (export "nanotime") (result i64) (local $s i32)
64+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.const 0)))
65+ (drop (call $clock_time_get (i32.const 1) (i64.const 0) (local.get $s)))
66+ (i64.load (local.get $s)))
67+ ;; one relative clock subscription: subscription 48 bytes @s, event 32
68+ ;; bytes @s+48, nevents @s+80
69+ (func (export "sleep") (param $ms i64) (local $s i32)
70+ (if (i64.le_s (local.get $ms) (i64.const 0)) (then (return)))
71+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.const 0)))

73+ (i32.store offset=16 (local.get $s) (i32.const 1)) ;; tag 0 = clock; id 1 = monotonic
74+ (i64.store offset=24 (local.get $s) (i64.mul (local.get $ms) (i64.const 1000000)))
75+ (drop (call $poll_oneoff (local.get $s) (i32.add (local.get $s) (i32.const 48)) (i32.const 1)

78+ (func (export "read_key") (param $buf i32) (param $cap i32) (result i32) (local $s i32)
79+ (if (i32.eqz (local.get $cap)) (then (return (i32.const 0))))
80+ (local.set $s (call $scratch (i32.add (local.get $buf) (local.get $cap))))
81+ (i32.store (local.get $s) (local.get $buf))
82+ (i32.store offset=4 (local.get $s) (i32.const 1))
83+ (i32.store offset=8 (local.get $s) (i32.const 0))
84+ (drop (call $fd_read (i32.const 0) (local.get $s) (i32.const 1) (i32.add (local.get $s) (i32.const 8))))
85+ (i32.load offset=8 (local.get $s)))
86+ ;; a non-blocking peek would need poll_oneoff on fd 0; not done here,
87+ ;; so this host always reports "nothing pending"
88+ (func (export "key_pending") (result i32) (i32.const 0))
89+ (func (export "size") (result i32 i32) (i32.const 80) (i32.const 24)))

1+// xsofy-shell-adapter.js — window.LetGoHost backed by lg-wasm-host.js, so
2+// xsofy/tools/xsofy-shell.html runs a lower-wasm module unchanged (P4.1).
3+//
4+// A CLASSIC script, loaded before the shell is injected: the shell calls
5+// window.LetGoHost.onReady at parse time, so the surface must exist before
6+// any module script could run. It takes the place of let-go's lg-host-core.js
7+// in a `lg -w -w-shell none` bundle and keeps its shape: onReady(cb),
8+// onOutput(cb), onEmit(cb), sendInput(str), setSize(c, r). The host module is
9+// pulled in with a dynamic import.
10+//
11+// ?module=<url> names the .wasm (default module.wasm). window.__lgw is what
12+// checks/browser-boot.mjs reads back.
13+(function () {
14+ let outputSink = null; const outputBuffer = [];
15+ let readyCb = null, readyMode = null;
16+ let emitSink = (name, data) => window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(name, { detail: data }));
17+ let host = null;
18+ let sized = null; // resolves on the shell's first setSize
19+ const firstSize = new Promise((r) => { sized = r; });
20+ const url = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('module') || 'module.wasm';
21+ const result = window.__lgw = { module: url, stdout: '', stderr: '', done: false,
22+ readyMode: null, size: null, sent: 0, dropped: 0 };
23+
24+ window.LetGoHost = {
25+ onReady(cb) { readyCb = cb; if (readyMode !== null) cb(readyMode); },
26+ onOutput(cb) { outputSink = cb; for (const s of outputBuffer.splice(0)) cb(s); },
27+ onEmit(cb) { emitSink = cb; },
28+ sendInput(s) {
29+ const ok = host ? host.sendInput(s) : false;
30+ if (ok) result.sent++; else result.dropped++;
31+ return ok;
32+ },
33+ setSize(c, r) {
34+ result.size = [c | 0, r | 0];
35+ if (host) host.setSize(c, r);
36+ sized();
37+ },
38+ };
39+ const output = (s) => {
40+ if (result.tShellFirstOutput === undefined) result.tShellFirstOutput = performance.now();
41+ if (outputSink) outputSink(s); else outputBuffer.push(s);
42+ };
43+ const ready = (mode) => { readyMode = result.readyMode = mode; if (readyCb) readyCb(mode); };
44+
45+ const base = document.currentScript.src;
46+ (async () => {
47+ try {
48+ const { LgWasmHost, hasJSPI } = await import(new URL('lg-wasm-host.js', base).href);
49+ result.jspi = hasJSPI; result.coi = self.crossOriginIsolated === true;
50+ const bytes = await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer();
51+ host = new LgWasmHost({
52+ urlParams: new URLSearchParams(location.search),
53+ // let-go's main-thread _lgEmit: parse the JSON, hand it to the sink,
54+ // which by default fires the window CustomEvent the shell listens for
55+ onEmit(name, json) {
56+ try { emitSink(name, JSON.parse(json)); } catch (e) { console.error('emit', name, e); }
57+ },
58+ onOutput(text, fd) {
59+ if (fd === 2) result.stderr += text; else result.stdout += text;
60+ output(text);
61+ },
62+ });
63+ // 'worker', not 'jspi': xsofy-shell.html binds setSize / onData /
64+ // sendInput only when mode === 'worker' (D90, host/ABI.md). Input here
65+ // is a parked JSPI stack, not let-go's worker + SAB ring, but the shell
66+ // only needs to know that input is live.
67+ ready('worker');
68+ // The shell opens xterm (after awaiting its font) and only then calls
69+ // setSize. Start the program after that, or a fast module reads the
70+ // 80x24 default before the real grid exists. A shell that never calls
71+ // setSize gets the default after 2 s.
72+ await Promise.race([firstSize, new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000))]);
73+ result.tMainStart = performance.now();
74+ const r = await host.run(bytes);
75+ Object.assign(result, r, { tDone: performance.now() });
76+ } catch (e) {
77+ Object.assign(result, { code: -1, error: String((e && e.message) || e) });
78+ output(`\r\nlower-wasm host error: ${result.error}\r\n`);
79+ }
80+ result.done = true;
81+ })();
82+})();
